 120    def get_access(self, default: str = None) -> str:
 121        """
 122
 123        The function `get_access` retrieves the access level from the parameters or configuration,
 124        returning a default value if not found.
 125        :param default: The `default` parameter in the `get_access` function is used to specify a default
 126        access level to return if the access level is not found in either the parameters or the
 127        configuration. If the access level is not found in both places, the function will return the
 128        value of the `default` parameter
 129        :type default: str
 130
 131        :return: The method `get_access` is returning a string value that represents the access level.
 132        """
 133
 134        # Find access in param then in config, otherwise return default
 135        return self.get_param().get("access", self.get_config().get("access", default))

 150    def load_header(
 151        self,
 152        header=None,
 153        table: str = None,
 154        drop: bool = False,
 155        view_name: str = "header",
 156    ) -> str:
 157        """
 158        Load header in a table, with INFO, FORMAT, FILTERS, SAMPLES and METADATA
 159
 160        Args:
 161            header (vcfobject, optional): VCF object from pyVCF. Defaults to None (header of the Variants object).
 162            table (str, optional): Table name of the header table. Defaults to None (defined as 'header' later).
 163            drop (bool, optional): Drop table if exists. Defaults to False.
 164            view_name (str, optional): Name of the table. Defaults to 'header'.
 165
 166        Returns:
 167            str: Name of the table, None otherwise
 168
 169        """
 170
 171        def create_header_table(conn):
 172            """
 173            Create header table
 174
 175            Args:
 176                conn (conn): Database connexion.
 177
 178            """
 179
 180            # Columns
 181            columns = [
 182                "section VARCHAR",
 183                "id VARCHAR",
 184                "number VARCHAR",
 185                "type VARCHAR",
 186                "description VARCHAR",
 187            ]
 188
 189            # Query create
 190            query_create = f"""
 191            CREATE OR REPLACE table {view_name} (
 192                {', '.join(columns)},
 193                PRIMARY KEY (section, id)
 194            );
 195            """
 196
 197            # Execute
 198            conn.execute(query_create)
 199
 200        def insert_header(conn, vcf_header):
 201            """
 202            Insert header into table
 203
 204            Args:
 205                conn (conn): Database connexion.
 206
 207            """
 208
 209            # Init
 210            inserts = []
 211
 212            # Add INFO section
 213            for info_id, info in vcf_header.infos.items():
 214                inserts.append(
 215                    (
 216                        "INFO",
 217                        info_id,
 218                        str(info.num if info.num is not None else "."),
 219                        info.type if info.type is not None else "",
 220                        info.desc if info.desc is not None else "",
 221                    )
 222                )
 223
 224            # Add FORMAT section
 225            for format_id, format in vcf_header.formats.items():
 226                inserts.append(
 227                    (
 228                        "FORMAT",
 229                        format_id,
 230                        str(format.num if format.num is not None else "."),
 231                        format.type if format.type is not None else "",
 232                        format.desc if format.desc is not None else "",
 233                    )
 234                )
 235
 236            # Add FILTER section
 237            for filter_id, filter in vcf_header.filters.items():
 238                inserts.append(
 239                    (
 240                        "FILTER",
 241                        filter_id,
 242                        "",
 243                        "",
 244                        filter.desc if filter.desc is not None else "",
 245                    )
 246                )
 247
 248            # Add Samples
 249            for sample_id in vcf_header.samples:
 250                inserts.append(
 251                    (
 252                        "SAMPLE",
 253                        sample_id,
 254                        "",
 255                        "",
 256                        "",
 257                    )
 258                )
 259
 260            # Add Metadata
 261            for key, value in vcf_header.metadata.items():
 262                inserts.append(
 263                    (
 264                        "METADATA",
 265                        key,
 266                        "",
 267                        "",
 268                        str(value) if value is not None else "",
 269                    )
 270                )
 271
 272            # Create query of insert with parameters
 273            query_insert = f"""
 274            INSERT INTO {view_name} (section, id, number, type, description) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?);
 275            """
 276            conn.executemany(query_insert, inserts)
 277
 278        # Get header is None
 279        if header is None:
 280            header = self.get_header()
 281
 282        # Header table
 283        if table is None:
 284            table = "header"
 285
 286        # If header is not None
 287        if header is not None:
 288
 289            # Connexion
 290            conn = self.get_connexion()
 291
 292            # Drop table
 293            if drop:
 294                query_drop = f"""
 295                DROP TABLE IF EXISTS {table}
 296                """
 297                conn.execute(query_drop)
 298
 299            # Create table
 300            create_header_table(conn)
 301            insert_header(conn, header)
 302
 303            return table
 304
 305        else:
 306
 307            return None

 309    def set_samples(self, samples: list = None) -> list:
 310        """
 311        The function `set_samples` sets the samples attribute of an object to a provided list or
 312        retrieves it from a parameter dictionary.
 313
 314        :param samples: The `set_samples` method is a method of a class that takes a list of samples as
 315        input and sets the `samples` attribute of the class to the provided list. If no samples are
 316        provided, it tries to get the samples from the class's parameters using the `get_param` method
 317        :type samples: list
 318        :return: The `samples` list is being returned.

 320

 431    def get_connexion_config(self) -> dict:
 432        """
 433        The function `get_connexion_config` returns a dictionary containing the configuration for a
 434        connection, including the number of threads and memory limit.
 435        :return: a dictionary containing the configuration for the Connexion library.
 436        """
 437
 438        # config
 439        config = self.get_config()
 440
 441        # Connexion config
 442        connexion_config = {}
 443        threads = self.get_threads()
 444
 445        # Threads
 446        if threads:
 447            connexion_config["threads"] = threads
 448
 449        # Memory
 450        # if config.get("memory", None):
 451        #     connexion_config["memory_limit"] = config.get("memory")
 452        if self.get_memory():
 453            connexion_config["memory_limit"] = self.get_memory()
 454
 455        # Temporary directory
 456        if config.get("temp_directory", None):
 457            connexion_config["temp_directory"] = config.get("temp_directory")
 458        else:
 459            config["temp_directory"] = os.path.join(
 460                self.get_tmp_dir(), f"duckdb_temp_" + get_random(10)
 461            )
 462            self.set_config(config)
 463            connexion_config["temp_directory"] = config["temp_directory"]
 464
 465        # Access
 466        access = self.get_access(default=None)
 467        if access:
 468            access_mode = access
 469            if access in ["RO"]:
 470                access_mode = "READ_ONLY"
 471            elif access in ["RW"]:
 472                access_mode = "READ_WRITE"
 473            connexion_db = self.get_connexion_db()
 474            if connexion_db in ":memory:":
 475                access_mode = "READ_WRITE"
 476            connexion_config["access_mode"] = access_mode
 477
 478        return connexion_config

 480    def get_duckdb_settings(self) -> dict:
 481        """
 482        The function `get_duckdb_settings` retrieves DuckDB settings from a configuration file or a

 484        :return: The function `get_duckdb_settings` returns a dictionary object `duckdb_settings_dict`.

 486
 487        # config

 489
 490        # duckdb settings
 491        duckdb_settings_dict = {}
 492        if config.get("duckdb_settings", None):
 493            duckdb_settings = config.get("duckdb_settings")
 494            duckdb_settings = full_path(duckdb_settings)
 495            # duckdb setting is a file
 496            if os.path.exists(duckdb_settings):
 497                with open(duckdb_settings) as json_file:
 498                    duckdb_settings_dict = yaml.safe_load(json_file)
 499            # duckdb settings is a string
 500            else:
 501                duckdb_settings_dict = json.loads(duckdb_settings)
 502
 503        return duckdb_settings_dict

 505    def set_connexion_db(self) -> str:
 506        """
 507        The function `set_connexion_db` returns the appropriate database connection string based on the
 508        input format and connection type.
 509        :return: the value of the variable `connexion_db`.
 510        """
 511
 512        # Default connexion db
 513        default_connexion_db = ":memory:"
 514
 515        # Find connexion db
 516        if self.get_input_format() in ["db", "duckdb"]:
 517            connexion_db = self.get_input()
 518        elif self.get_connexion_type() in ["memory", default_connexion_db, None]:
 519            connexion_db = default_connexion_db
 520        elif self.get_connexion_type() in ["tmpfile"]:
 521            connexion_db = self.get_tmp_dir() + f"/howard.{get_random()}.tmp.db"
 522        elif self.get_connexion_type() != "":
 523            connexion_db = self.get_connexion_type()
 524        else:
 525            connexion_db = default_connexion_db
 526
 527        # Set connexion db
 528        self.connexion_db = connexion_db
 529
 530        return connexion_db

 532    def set_connexion(self, conn) -> None:
 533        """
 534        The function `set_connexion` creates a connection to a database, with options for different
 535        database formats and settings.
 536
 537        :param conn: The `conn` parameter in the `set_connexion` method is the connection to the
 538        database. If a connection is not provided, a new connection to an in-memory database is created.
 539        The method then proceeds to set up the connection based on the specified format (e.g., duckdb or
 540        sqlite
 541        """
 542
 543        # Connexion db
 544        connexion_db = self.set_connexion_db()
 545
 546        # Connexion config
 547        connexion_config = self.get_connexion_config()
 548
 549        # Connexion format
 550        connexion_format = self.get_config().get("connexion_format", "duckdb")
 551        # Set connexion format
 552        self.connexion_format = connexion_format
 553
 554        # Connexion
 555        if not conn:
 556            if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
 557                conn = duckdb.connect(connexion_db, config=connexion_config)
 558                # duckDB settings
 559                duckdb_settings = self.get_duckdb_settings()
 560                if duckdb_settings:
 561                    for setting in duckdb_settings:
 562                        setting_value = duckdb_settings.get(setting)
 563                        if isinstance(setting_value, str):
 564                            setting_value = f"'{setting_value}'"
 565                        conn.execute(f"PRAGMA {setting}={setting_value};")
 566                # duckDB settings arrow large buffer size
 567                conn.execute("SET arrow_large_buffer_size=true")
 568                # settings = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM duckdb_settings()").df()
 569                # log.debug(f"DuckDB settings after connexion:\n{settings.to_string()}")
 570            elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
 571                conn = sqlite3.connect(connexion_db)
 572
 573        # Set connexion
 574        self.conn = conn
 575
 576        # Log
 577        log.debug(f"connexion_format: {connexion_format}")
 578        log.debug(f"connexion_db: {connexion_db}")
 579        log.debug(f"connexion config: {connexion_config}")
 580        log.debug(f"connexion duckdb settings: {self.get_duckdb_settings()}")
 581        log.debug("connexion duckdb settings: arrow_large_buffer_size=true")
 582

 610    def set_header(self) -> None:
 611        """
 612        It reads the header of a VCF file and stores it as a list of strings and as a VCF object
 613        """
 614
 615        input_file = self.get_input()
 616        default_header_list = [
 617            "##fileformat=VCFv4.2",
 618            "#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT	QUAL	FILTER	INFO",
 619        ]
 620
 621        # Full path
 622        input_file = full_path(input_file)
 623
 624        if input_file:
 625
 626            input_format = self.get_input_format()
 627            input_compressed = self.get_input_compressed()
 628            config = self.get_config()
 629            header_list = default_header_list
 630            if input_format in [
 631                "vcf",
 632                "hdr",
 633                "tsv",
 634                "csv",
 635                "psv",
 636                "parquet",
 637                "db",
 638                "duckdb",
 639                "json",
 640            ]:
 641                # header provided in param
 642                if config.get("header_file", None):
 643                    with open(config.get("header_file"), "rt") as f:
 644                        header_list = self.read_vcf_header(f)
 645                # within a vcf file format (header within input file itsself)
 646                elif input_format in ["vcf", "hdr"] and not os.path.isdir(input_file):
 647                    # within a compressed vcf file format (.vcf.gz)
 648                    if input_compressed:
 649                        with bgzf.open(input_file, "rt") as f:
 650                            header_list = self.read_vcf_header(f)
 651                    # within an uncompressed vcf file format (.vcf)
 652                    else:
 653                        with open(input_file, "rt") as f:
 654                            header_list = self.read_vcf_header(f)
 655                # header provided in default external file .hdr
 656                elif os.path.exists((input_file + ".hdr")):
 657                    with open(input_file + ".hdr", "rt") as f:
 658                        header_list = self.read_vcf_header(f)
 659                else:
 660                    try:  # Try to get header info fields and file columns
 661
 662                        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
 663
 664                            # Create database
 665                            db_for_header = Database(database=input_file)
 666
 667                            # Get header columns for infos fields
 668                            db_header_from_columns = (
 669                                db_for_header.get_header_from_columns()
 670                            )
 671
 672                            # Get real columns in the file
 673                            db_header_columns = db_for_header.get_columns()
 674
 675                            # Write header file
 676                            header_file_tmp = os.path.join(tmpdir, "header")
 677                            f = open(header_file_tmp, "w")
 678                            vcf.Writer(f, db_header_from_columns)
 679                            f.close()
 680
 681                            # Replace #CHROM line with rel columns
 682                            header_list = db_for_header.read_header_file(
 683                                header_file=header_file_tmp
 684                            )
 685                            header_list[-1] = "\t".join(db_header_columns)
 686
 687                    except:
 688
 689                        log.warning(
 690                            f"No header for file {input_file}. Set as default VCF header"
 691                        )
 692                        header_list = default_header_list
 693
 694            else:  # try for unknown format ?
 695
 696                log.error(f"Input file format '{input_format}' not available")
 697                raise ValueError(f"Input file format '{input_format}' not available")
 698
 699            if not header_list:
 700                header_list = default_header_list
 701
 702            # header as list
 703            self.header_list = header_list
 704
 705            # header as VCF object
 706            self.header_vcf = vcf.Reader(io.StringIO("\n".join(header_list)))
 707
 708        else:
 709
 710            self.header_list = None
 711            self.header_vcf = None
 712
 713    def get_query_to_df(self, query: str = "", limit: int = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
 714        """
 715        The `get_query_to_df` function takes a query as a string and returns the result as a pandas
 716        DataFrame based on the connection format. It supports both limited and full queries.
 717
 718        :param query: The `query` parameter in the `get_query_to_df` function is a string that
 719        represents the SQL query you want to execute. This query will be used to fetch data from a
 720        database and convert it into a pandas DataFrame
 721        :type query: str
 722        :param limit: The `limit` parameter in the `get_query_to_df` function is used to specify the
 723        maximum number of rows to be returned in the resulting dataframe. If a limit is provided, the
 724        function will only fetch up to that number of rows from the database query result. If no limit
 725        is specified,
 726        :type limit: int
 727        :return: A pandas DataFrame is being returned by the `get_query_to_df` function.
 728        """
 729
 730        # Connexion format
 731        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
 732
 733        # Limit in query
 734        if limit:
 735
 736            # Panda settings
 737            pd.set_option("display.max_rows", limit)
 738
 739            # DuckDB connexion
 740            if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
 741
 742                result = self.get_connexion().execute(query).fetch_record_batch(limit)
 743                if result is None:
 744                    df = result.df()
 745                else:
 746                    try:
 747                        df = result.read_next_batch().to_pandas()
 748                    except StopIteration:
 749                        df = self.get_connexion().execute(query).df()[0:limit]
 750
 751            # SQLite connexion
 752            elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
 753                df = next(pd.read_sql_query(query, self.conn, chunksize=limit))
 754
 755        # Full query without limit
 756        else:
 757
 758            # DuckDB connexion
 759            if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
 760                df = self.get_connexion().execute(query).df()
 761
 762            # SQLite connexion
 763            elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
 764                df = pd.read_sql_query(query, self.conn)
 765
 766        return df
 767
 768    def get_overview(self) -> None:
 769        """
 770        The function prints the input, output, config, and dataframe of the current object
 771        """
 772        table_variants_from = self.get_table_variants(clause="from")
 773        sql_columns = self.get_header_columns_as_sql()
 774        sql_query_export = f"SELECT {sql_columns} FROM {table_variants_from}"
 775        df = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_export)
 776        log.info(
 777            "Input:  "
 778            + str(self.get_input())
 779            + " ["
 780            + str(str(self.get_input_format()))
 781            + "]"
 782        )
 783        log.info(
 784            "Output: "
 785            + str(self.get_output())
 786            + " ["
 787            + str(str(self.get_output_format()))
 788            + "]"
 789        )
 790        log.info("Config: ")
 791        for d in str(json.dumps(self.get_config(), indent=4, sort_keys=True)).split(
 792            "\n"
 793        ):
 794            log.info("\t" + str(d))
 795        log.info("Param: ")
 796        for d in str(json.dumps(self.get_param(), indent=4, sort_keys=True)).split(
 797            "\n"
 798        ):
 799            log.info("\t" + str(d))
 800        log.info("Sample list: " + str(self.get_header_sample_list()))
 801        log.info("Dataframe: ")
 802        for d in str(df).split("\n"):
 803            log.info("\t" + str(d))
 804
 805        # garbage collector
 806        del df
 807        gc.collect()
 808
 809        return None

 811    def get_stats(
 812        self,
 813        table: str = None,
 814        table_view: str = None,
 815        annotations_stats: bool = False,
 816        queries: dict = None,
 817        queries_view: str = None,
 818    ) -> dict:
 819        """
 820        Calculate and return various statistics of the current object, including information about the input file,
 821        variants, samples, header fields, quality, and SNVs/InDels.
 822
 823        :param table: The name of the table containing variant data. If not provided, the default table is used.
 824        :type table: str, optional
 825        :param table_view: The name of the table view to be used for statistics calculation. If not provided, a new view is created.
 826        :type table_view: str, optional
 827        :param annotations_stats: Whether to calculate annotation statistics. Defaults to False.
 828        :type annotations_stats: bool, optional
 829        :param queries: The `queries` parameter is a dictionary that contains queries to be executed
 830        and added to the statistics. The keys of the dictionary are the names of the queries, and the
 831        values are the SQL queries to be executed.
 832        :type queries: dict
 833        :param queries_view: The `queries_view` parameter is a string that represents the name of the
 834        view to be used for the queries. If no value is provided, a new view will be created.
 835        :type queries_view: str
 836
 837        :return: A dictionary containing various statistics of the current object. The dictionary has the following structure:
 838
 839            - **Infos** (*dict*): General information about the input file and header fields.
 840                - **Input file** (*str*): The path to the input file.
 841                - **Header Infos** (*list*): List of INFO fields in the header.
 842                - **Header Formats** (*list*): List of FORMAT fields in the header.
 843                - **Number of INFO fields** (*int*): Number of INFO fields in the header.
 844                - **Number of FORMAT fields** (*int*): Number of FORMAT fields in the header.
 845                - **Number of samples** (*int*): Number of samples in the dataset.
 846                - **Number of variants** (*int*): Total number of variants in the dataset.
 847
 848            - **Variants** (*dict*): Statistics about the variants.
 849                - **By Chromosome** (*list*): List of dictionaries with chromosome names and variant counts.
 850                - **By Type** (*list*): List of dictionaries with variant types and counts.
 851                - **By Quality** (*list*): List of dictionaries with quality scores and counts.
 852                - **By Filter** (*list*): List of dictionaries with filter values and counts.
 853
 854            - **Samples** (*dict*): Statistics about the samples.
 855                - **Variants in samples** (*list*): List of dictionaries with sample names, variant counts, and percentages.
 856
 857            - **Header** (*dict*): Detailed information about the header fields.
 858                - **List of INFO fields** (*dict*): Dictionary with detailed information about INFO fields.
 859                - **List of FORMAT fields** (*dict*): Dictionary with detailed information about FORMAT fields.
 860                - **List of FILTER fields** (*dict*): Dictionary with detailed information about FILTER fields.
 861
 862            - **Annotations** (*dict*, optional): Annotation statistics, if `annotations_stats` is True.
 863                - **Stats** (*dict*): Dictionary with annotation statistics.
 864
 865            - **Quality** (*dict*): Quality statistics.
 866                - **QUAL** (*dict*): Dictionary with quality statistics (average, minimum, maximum, standard deviation, median, variance).
 867
 868        :rtype: dict
 869
 870        :example:
 871
 872        .. code-block:: python
 873
 874            stats = get_stats(table="variants_table", table_view="variants_view", annotations_stats=True)
 875            print(stats)
 876        """
 877
 878        # Log
 879        log.info(f"Stats Calculation...")
 880
 881        # table variants
 882        if table is None:
 883            table_variants_from = self.get_table_variants()
 884        else:
 885            table_variants_from = table
 886
 887        # table view
 888        if table_view is None:
 889            variants_view_stats_name = "variants_view_stats_" + get_random()
 890        else:
 891            variants_view_stats_name = table_view
 892
 893        # Tables to remove
 894        tables_to_remove = []
 895
 896        # Percent_round
 897        percent_round = 2
 898
 899        # Sample struct column name
 900        sample_struct_column = "SAMPLES"
 901
 902        # Info struct column name
 903        info_struct_column = None
 904
 905        # Sample struct column format needed
 906        if annotations_stats:
 907            info_prefix_column = ""
 908        else:
 909            info_prefix_column = None
 910
 911        # Create view
 912        variants_view_stats_name = self.create_annotations_view(
 913            table=table_variants_from,
 914            view=variants_view_stats_name,
 915            view_type="table",
 916            view_mode="full",
 917            info_prefix_column=info_prefix_column,
 918            info_struct_column=info_struct_column,
 919            sample_struct_column=sample_struct_column,
 920            formats=["GT"],
 921            fields_needed=[
 922                "#CHROM",
 923                "POS",
 924                "REF",
 925                "ALT",
 926                "QUAL",
 927                "FILTER",
 928            ]
 929            + self.get_header_sample_list(),
 930        )
 931        tables_to_remove.append(variants_view_stats_name)
 932
 933        # stats dict
 934        stats = {"Infos": {}}
 935
 936        ### File
 937        input_file = self.get_input()
 938        stats["Infos"]["Input file"] = input_file
 939
 940        # Header
 941        header_infos = self.get_header().infos
 942        header_formats = self.get_header().formats
 943        header_infos_list = list(header_infos)
 944        header_formats_list = list(header_formats)
 945        header_table = self.load_header()
 946
 947        # Stat section
 948        stats["Stats"] = {}
 949
 950        ### Variants
 951
 952        # Variants by chr
 953        sql_query_nb_variant_by_chrom = f'SELECT "#CHROM" as CHROM, count(*) as count FROM {variants_view_stats_name} GROUP BY "#CHROM"'
 954        df_nb_of_variants_by_chrom = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_nb_variant_by_chrom)
 955        nb_of_variants_by_chrom = df_nb_of_variants_by_chrom.sort_values(
 956            by=["CHROM"], kind="quicksort"
 957        )
 958
 959        # Total number of variants
 960        nb_of_variants = nb_of_variants_by_chrom["count"].sum()
 961
 962        # Calculate percentage
 963        nb_of_variants_by_chrom["percent"] = nb_of_variants_by_chrom["count"].apply(
 964            lambda x: round((x * 100 / nb_of_variants), percent_round)
 965        )
 966
 967        # Add to stats dict the number of variants by chromosome and the total number of variants
 968        stats["Stats"]["Variants by chromosome"] = nb_of_variants_by_chrom.to_dict(
 969            orient="index"
 970        )
 971
 972        # Add to stats dict the total number of variants
 973        stats["Infos"]["Number of variants"] = int(nb_of_variants)
 974
 975        ### Samples
 976
 977        # Init
 978        samples = {}
 979        nb_of_samples = 0
 980
 981        # Check Samples
 982        if "GT" in header_formats_list and "FORMAT" in self.get_header_columns():
 983            log.debug(f"Check samples...")
 984
 985            # Samples stats
 986            samples_stats = {}
 987
 988            # Get samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
 989            for sample in self.get_header_sample_list():
 990                sql_query_samples = f"""
 991                    SELECT 
 992                        '{sample}' as 'sample',
 993                        SAMPLES."{sample}".GT as 'genotype',
 994                        count(SAMPLES."{sample}".GT) as 'count',
 995                        ROUND((count(SAMPLES."{sample}".GT)*100/{nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) as 'percent'
 996                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
 997                    WHERE  SAMPLES."{sample}".GT IS NOT NULL
 998                    GROUP BY genotype
 999                    ORDER BY genotype
1000                """
1001
1002                # Get samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1003                sql_query_genotype_df = self.get_connexion().execute(sql_query_samples).df()
1004                non_null_genotypes = sql_query_genotype_df[
1005                    sql_query_genotype_df["genotype"].str.contains(r"\d")
1006                ]
1007                sample_genotype_count = non_null_genotypes["count"].sum()
1008
1009                # Add to samples dict the samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1010                if len(sql_query_genotype_df):
1011
1012                    # Number of samples
1013                    nb_of_samples += 1
1014
1015                    # Add to samples dict the samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1016                    samples[sample] = sql_query_genotype_df.to_dict(orient="index")
1017
1018                    # Add to samples stats dict the samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1019                    samples_stats[sample] = {
1020                        "Sample": f"{sample}",
1021                        "count": int(sample_genotype_count),
1022                        "percent": round(
1023                            (sample_genotype_count * 100 / nb_of_variants),
1024                            percent_round,
1025                        ),
1026                    }
1027
1028            # Add to stats dict the samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1029            stats["Samples"] = samples
1030            stats["Infos"]["Number of samples"] = nb_of_samples
1031            stats["Stats"]["Variants by sample"] = samples_stats
1032
1033        else:
1034
1035            samples_stats = {}
1036
1037        ### INFO and FORMAT fields
1038        header_types_df = {}
1039        header_types_list = {
1040            "INFO": {
1041                "label": "List of INFO fields",
1042                "fields": {
1043                    "id": "INFO",
1044                    "number": "Number",
1045                    "type": "Type",
1046                    "description": "Description",
1047                },
1048            },
1049            "FORMAT": {
1050                "label": "List of FORMAT fields",
1051                "fields": {
1052                    "id": "FORMAT",
1053                    "number": "Number",
1054                    "type": "Type",
1055                    "description": "Description",
1056                },
1057            },
1058            "FILTER": {
1059                "label": "List of FILTER fields",
1060                "fields": {
1061                    "id": "FILTER",
1062                    "description": "Description",
1063                },
1064            },
1065        }
1066
1067        # Init
1068        header_types_df = {}
1069
1070        # Get header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1071        for header_section, header_info in header_types_list.items():
1072            label = header_info["label"]
1073            fields = header_info["fields"]
1074
1075            # Construire la liste des champs à sélectionner
1076            select_fields = ", ".join(fields.keys())
1077
1078            # SQL query
1079            sql_query_header = f"""
1080                SELECT {select_fields}
1081                FROM {header_table}
1082                WHERE section = '{header_section}'
1083            """
1084            header_infos_df = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_header)
1085            header_infos_dict = {}
1086
1087            # Add to header_types_df the header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1088            for i, row in header_infos_df.iterrows():
1089                header_infos_dict[i] = {
1090                    new if new else original: row[original]
1091                    for original, new in fields.items()
1092                }
1093
1094            # Add to header_types_df the header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1095            if len(header_infos_dict):
1096
1097                # Add to header_types_df the header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1098                header_types_df[label] = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(
1099                    header_infos_dict, orient="index"
1100                ).to_dict(orient="index")
1101
1102                # Add to stats dict the number of INFO and FORMAT fields
1103                stats["Infos"][f"Number of {header_section} fields"] = len(
1104                    header_types_df[label]
1105                )
1106
1107        # Add to stats dict the header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1108        stats["Header"] = header_types_df
1109
1110        # Annotations stats
1111        if annotations_stats:
1112
1113            # Init
1114            sql_queries_info = []
1115
1116            # Get header infos list
1117            for field in header_infos_list:
1118
1119                # Create a table with a field by line (only for INFO section), and le number of distinct value on variants table, and the number of variants with a value
1120                sql_queries_info.append(f"""
1121                        SELECT
1122                            '{field}' AS 'Annotation',
1123                            count(distinct "{field}") as 'Distinct values',
1124                            count("{field}") as 'Annotated Variants',
1125                            ROUND((count("{field}") * 100 / {nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) as 'Percent',
1126                        FROM
1127                            {variants_view_stats_name}
1128                        WHERE
1129                            "{field}" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(CAST("{field}" AS VARCHAR)) NOT IN ('','.')
1130                    """)
1131
1132            # Join all queries
1133            sql_query_info = f""" UNION ALL """.join(sql_queries_info)
1134
1135            # Get info stats
1136            info_stats = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_info)
1137
1138            # Add to stats dict the annotations stats
1139            stats["Annotations"] = {"Distribution": info_stats.to_dict(orient="index")}
1140
1141        ### Quality stats
1142        log.debug(f"Quality stats...")
1143
1144        ### QUAL
1145        log.debug(f"Quality stats: QUAL...")
1146
1147        if "QUAL" in self.get_header_columns():
1148
1149            # SQL query
1150            sql_query_qual = f"""
1151                    SELECT
1152                        avg(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Average,
1153                        min(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Minimum,
1154                        max(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Maximum,
1155                        stddev(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS StandardDeviation,
1156                        median(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Median,
1157                        variance(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Variance
1158                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1159                    WHERE CAST(QUAL AS VARCHAR) NOT IN ('.')
1160                    """
1161
1162            # Get quality stats
1163            qual_stats = self.get_connexion().execute(sql_query_qual).df().to_dict(orient="index")
1164
1165        else:
1166
1167            # Empty quality stats
1168            qual_stats = {}
1169
1170        ### FILTER
1171        log.debug(f"Quality stats: FILTER...")
1172
1173        if "FILTER" in self.get_header_columns():
1174
1175            # SQL query
1176            sql_query_filter = f"""
1177                WITH split_filter AS (
1178                    SELECT
1179                        TRIM(UNNEST(STRING_SPLIT(CASE WHEN TRIM(FILTER) = '' OR FILTER IS NULL THEN '.' ELSE FILTER END, ';'))) AS filter_value
1180                    FROM
1181                        {variants_view_stats_name}
1182                )
1183                SELECT
1184                    filter_value,
1185                    COUNT(*) AS 'count',
1186                    ROUND((count * 100 / {nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) AS 'percent'
1187                FROM
1188                    split_filter
1189                GROUP BY
1190                    filter_value
1191                ORDER BY
1192                    count DESC
1193            """
1194
1195            # Get filter stats
1196            filter_stats = (
1197                self.get_connexion().execute(sql_query_filter).df().to_dict(orient="index")
1198            )
1199
1200        else:
1201
1202            # Empty filter stats
1203            filter_stats = {}
1204
1205        ### SNV and InDel
1206
1207        # SQL query
1208        sql_query_snv = f"""
1209            
1210            SELECT Type, count, ROUND((count * 100 / {nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) AS 'percent' FROM (
1211
1212                    SELECT
1213                        'Total' AS Type,
1214                        count(*) AS count
1215                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1216                    
1217                    UNION
1218
1219                    SELECT
1220                        'SNV' AS Type,
1221                        count(*) AS count
1222                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1223                    WHERE len(REF) = 1 AND len(ALT) = 1
1224
1225                    UNION
1226
1227                    SELECT
1228                        'MNV' AS Type,
1229                        count(*) AS count
1230                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1231                    WHERE len(REF) > 1 AND len(ALT) > 1
1232                    AND len(REF) = len(ALT)
1233
1234                    UNION
1235
1236                    SELECT
1237                        'InDel' AS Type,
1238                        count(*) AS count
1239                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1240                    WHERE len(REF) > 1 OR len(ALT) > 1
1241                    AND len(REF) != len(ALT)
1242
1243                )
1244
1245            ORDER BY 
1246            CASE
1247                WHEN Type = 'Total' THEN 1
1248                WHEN Type = 'SNV' THEN 2
1249                WHEN Type = 'MNV' THEN 3
1250                WHEN Type = 'InDel' THEN 4
1251            END
1252
1253                """
1254
1255        # Get SNV and InDel stats
1256        snv_indel = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_snv).to_dict(orient="index")
1257
1258        # Substitutions
1259        sql_query_snv_substitution = f"""
1260                SELECT
1261                    concat(REF, '>', ALT) AS 'Substitution',
1262                    count(*) AS count,
1263                    ROUND((count * 100 / {nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) AS 'percent'
1264                FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1265                WHERE len(REF) = 1 AND len(ALT) = 1
1266                GROUP BY REF, ALT
1267                ORDER BY count(*) DESC
1268                """
1269        snv_substitution = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_snv_substitution).to_dict(
1270            orient="index"
1271        )
1272
1273        # Add to stats dict the SNV and InDel stats
1274        stats["Stats"]["Variant types"] = snv_indel
1275        stats["Stats"]["Substitutions"] = snv_substitution
1276        stats["Stats"]["Quality"] = qual_stats
1277        stats["Stats"]["Filters"] = filter_stats
1278
1279        # Queries
1280        if queries is not None:
1281
1282            # Create full annotations view
1283            variants_view_query_name = queries_view
1284            variants_view_query_name = self.create_annotations_view(
1285                table=table_variants_from,
1286                view=variants_view_query_name,
1287                view_type="view",
1288                view_mode="explore",
1289                info_prefix_column="",
1290                info_struct_column="INFOS",
1291                sample_struct_column="SAMPLES",
1292                formats=None,
1293                fields_needed_all=True,
1294                drop_view=True,
1295            )
1296            if queries_view is not None:
1297                tables_to_remove.append(variants_view_query_name)
1298
1299            # Stats queries section
1300            stats["Queries"] = {}
1301
1302            # For each query
1303            for query_infos in queries.items():
1304
1305                # Query name and query
1306                query_name = query_infos[0]
1307                query = query_infos[1]
1308
1309                # Query cast
1310                query_cast = cast_columns_query(query=query, conn=self.get_connexion())
1311
1312                # Query execute
1313                query_res = self.get_query_to_df(query_cast).to_dict(orient="index")
1314                stats["Queries"][query_name] = query_res
1315
1316        # Remove table or view
1317        self.remove_tables_or_views(tables=tables_to_remove)
1318
1319        return stats
1320
1321    def stats_to_file(
1322        self,
1323        file: str = None,
1324        annotations_stats: bool = False,
1325        queries: dict = None,
1326        queries_view: str = None,
1327    ) -> str:
1328        """
1329        The function `stats_to_file` takes a file name as input, retrieves statistics, serializes them
1330        into a JSON object, and writes the JSON object to the specified file.
1331
1332        :param file: The `file` parameter is a string that represents the file path where the JSON data
1333        will be written
1334        :type file: str
1335        :param annotations_stats: The `annotations_stats` parameter is a boolean that specifies whether
1336        to calculate annotation statistics. If `annotations_stats` is set to True, annotation statistics
1337        will be calculated. If `annotations_stats` is set to False, annotation statistics will not be
1338        calculated. The default value is False.
1339        :type annotations_stats: bool
1340        :param queries: The `queries` parameter is a dictionary that contains queries to be executed
1341        and added to the statistics. The keys of the dictionary are the names of the queries, and the
1342        values are the SQL queries to be executed.
1343        :type queries: dict
1344        :param queries_view: The `queries_view` parameter is a string that represents the name of the
1345        view to be used for the queries. If no value is provided, a new view will be created.
1346        :type queries_view: str
1347
1348        :return: The name of the file that was written to.
1349        """
1350
1351        # Get stats
1352        stats = self.get_stats(
1353            annotations_stats=annotations_stats,
1354            queries=queries,
1355            queries_view=queries_view,
1356        )
1357
1358        # Serializing json
1359        json_object = json.dumps(stats, indent=4)
1360
1361        # Writing to sample.json
1362        with open(file, "w") as outfile:
1363            outfile.write(json_object)
1364
1365        return file

1367    def print_stats(
1368        self,
1369        stdout: bool = False,
1370        output_file: str = None,
1371        json_file: str = None,
1372        html_file: str = None,
1373        pdf_file: str = None,
1374        annotations_stats: bool = False,
1375        queries: dict = None,
1376        queries_view: str = None,
1377    ) -> None:
1378        """
1379        The `print_stats` function generates a markdown file and prints the statistics contained in a
1380        JSON file in a formatted manner.
1381
1382        :param stdout: The `stdout` parameter is a boolean that specifies whether to print the stats
1383        directly to the standard output. If `stdout` is set to True, the stats will be printed to the
1384        standard output. If `stdout` is set to False, the stats will not be printed to the standard
1385        output. The default value is False.
1386        :type stdout: bool
1387        :param output_file: The `output_file` parameter is a string that specifies the path and filename
1388        of the output file where the stats will be printed in Markdown format. If no `output_file` is
1389        provided, a temporary directory will be created and the stats will be saved in a file named
1390        "stats.md" within that
1391        :type output_file: str
1392        :param json_file: The `json_file` parameter is a string that represents the path to the JSON
1393        file where the statistics will be saved. If no value is provided, a temporary directory will be
1394        created and a default file name "stats.json" will be used
1395        :type json_file: str
1396        :param html_file: The `html_file` parameter is a string that specifies the path and filename of
1397        the output file where the stats will be printed in HTML format. If no `html_file` is provided,
1398        a temporary directory will be created and the stats will be saved in a file named "stats.html"
1399        within that
1400        :type html_file: str
1401        :param pdf_file: The `pdf_file` parameter is a string that specifies the path and filename of the
1402        output file where the stats will be printed in PDF format. If no `pdf_file` is provided, a
1403        temporary directory will be created and the stats will be saved in a file named "stats.pdf"
1404        within that
1405        :type pdf_file: str
1406        :param annotations_stats: Whether to calculate annotation statistics. Defaults to False.
1407        :type annotations_stats: bool, optional
1408        :param queries: The `queries` parameter is a dictionary that contains queries to be executed
1409        and added to the statistics. The keys of the dictionary are the names of the queries, and the
1410        values are the SQL queries to be executed.
1411        :type queries: dict
1412        :param queries_view: The `queries_view` parameter is a string that represents the name of the
1413        view to be used for the queries. If no value is provided, a new view will be created.
1414        :type queries_view: str
1415        of `None`.
1416
1417        :return: The function `print_stats` does not return any value. It has a return type annotation
1418
1419        """
1420
1421        # Full path
1422        output_file = full_path(output_file)
1423        json_file = full_path(json_file)
1424
1425        # Create stats file in temporary directory
1426        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
1427
1428            # Files
1429            if not output_file:
1430                output_file = os.path.join(tmpdir, "stats.md")
1431            if not json_file:
1432                json_file = os.path.join(tmpdir, "stats.json")
1433
1434            # Create folders
1435            if not os.path.exists(os.path.dirname(output_file)):
1436                Path(os.path.dirname(output_file)).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1437            if not os.path.exists(os.path.dirname(json_file)):
1438                Path(os.path.dirname(json_file)).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1439
1440            # Create stats JSON file
1441            stats_file = self.stats_to_file(
1442                file=json_file,
1443                annotations_stats=annotations_stats,
1444                queries=queries,
1445                queries_view=queries_view,
1446            )
1447
1448            # Print stats file
1449            with open(stats_file) as f:
1450                stats = yaml.safe_load(f)
1451
1452            # Output
1453            output_title = []
1454            output_index = []
1455            output = []
1456
1457            # Title
1458            output_title.append("# HOWARD Stats")
1459
1460            # Index
1461            output_index.append("## Table of context")
1462
1463            # Process sections
1464            for section in stats:
1465                infos = stats.get(section)
1466                section_link = "#" + section.lower().replace(" ", "-")
1467                output.append(f"\n")
1468                output.append(f"## {section}")
1469                output_index.append(f"- [{section}]({section_link})")
1470
1471                if len(infos):
1472
1473                    # For each info
1474                    for info in infos:
1475
1476                        # Check if dataframe or not
1477                        try:
1478                            df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(infos.get(info), orient="index")
1479                            is_df = True
1480                        except:
1481                            try:
1482                                df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(
1483                                    json.loads((infos.get(info))), orient="index"
1484                                )
1485                                is_df = True
1486                            except:
1487                                is_df = False
1488
1489                        # If dataframe is a dataframe
1490                        if is_df:
1491                            df = df.map(escape_markdown_table_chars)
1492                            output.append(f"### {info}")
1493                            info_link = "#" + info.lower().replace(" ", "-")
1494                            output_index.append(f"   - [{info}]({info_link})")
1495                            output.append(f"{df.to_markdown(index=False)}")
1496
1497                        # If not a dataframe
1498                        else:
1499                            output.append(f"- {info}: {infos.get(info)}")
1500
1501                else:
1502
1503                    # If no info
1504                    output.append(f"NA")
1505
1506            # Write stats in markdown file
1507            with open(output_file, "w") as fp:
1508                for item in output_title:
1509                    fp.write("%s\n" % item)
1510                fp.write("\n")
1511                for item in output_index:
1512                    fp.write("%s\n" % item)
1513                fp.write("\n")
1514                for item in output:
1515                    fp.write("%s\n" % item)
1516
1517            # Output stats in markdown
1518            if stdout:
1519                print("")
1520                print("\n\n".join(output_title))
1521                print("")
1522                print("\n\n".join(output))
1523                print("")
1524
1525            # Generate HTML and PDF files
1526            if html_file:
1527                convert_markdown_to_html(output_file, html_file)
1528            if pdf_file:
1529                convert_markdown_to_pdf(output_file, pdf_file)
1530
1531        return None

1654        else:

1656        return table_variants

1784    def get_header_sample_list(
1785        self, check: bool = False, samples: list = None, samples_force: bool = False
1786    ) -> list:
1787        """
1788        The function `get_header_sample_list` returns a list of samples from a VCF header, with optional
1789        checking and filtering based on input parameters.
1790
1791        :param check: The `check` parameter in the `get_header_sample_list` function is a boolean
1792        parameter that determines whether to check if the samples in the list are properly defined as
1793        genotype columns. If `check` is set to `True`, the function will verify if each sample in the
1794        list is defined as a, defaults to False
1795        :type check: bool (optional)
1796        :param samples: The `samples` parameter in the `get_header_sample_list` function is a list that
1797        allows you to specify a subset of samples from the header. If you provide a list of sample
1798        names, the function will check if each sample is defined in the header. If a sample is not found
1799        in the
1800        :type samples: list
1801        :param samples_force: The `samples_force` parameter in the `get_header_sample_list` function is
1802        a boolean parameter that determines whether to force the function to return the sample list
1803        without checking if the samples are genotype columns. If `samples_force` is set to `True`, the
1804        function will return the sample list without performing, defaults to False
1805        :type samples_force: bool (optional)
1806        :return: The function `get_header_sample_list` returns a list of samples based on the input
1807        parameters and conditions specified in the function.
1808        """
1809
1810        # Init
1811        samples_list = []
1812
1813        if samples is None:
1814            samples_list = self.header_vcf.samples
1815        else:
1816            samples_checked = []
1817            for sample in samples:
1818                if sample in self.header_vcf.samples:
1819                    samples_checked.append(sample)
1820                else:
1821                    log.warning(f"Sample '{sample}' not defined in header")
1822            samples_list = samples_checked
1823
1824            # Force sample list without checking if is_genotype_column
1825            if samples_force:
1826                log.warning(f"Samples {samples_list} not checked if genotypes")
1827                return samples_list
1828
1829        if check:
1830            samples_checked = []
1831            for sample in samples_list:
1832                if self.is_genotype_column(column=sample):
1833                    samples_checked.append(sample)
1834                else:
1835                    log.warning(
1836                        f"Sample '{sample}' not defined as a sample (genotype not well defined)"
1837                    )
1838            samples_list = samples_checked
1839
1840        # Return samples list
1841        return samples_list

1897    def insert_file_to_table(
1898        self,
1899        file,
1900        columns: str,
1901        header_len: int = 0,
1902        sep: str = "\t",
1903        chunksize: int = 1000000,
1904    ) -> None:
1905        """
1906        The function reads a file in chunks and inserts each chunk into a table based on the specified
1907        database format.
1908
1909        :param file: The `file` parameter is the file that you want to load into a table. It should be
1910        the path to the file on your system
1911        :param columns: The `columns` parameter in the `insert_file_to_table` function is a string that
1912        should contain the names of the columns in the table where the data will be inserted. The column
1913        names should be separated by commas within the string. For example, if you have columns named
1914        "id", "name
1915        :type columns: str
1916        :param header_len: The `header_len` parameter in the `insert_file_to_table` function specifies
1917        the number of lines to skip at the beginning of the file before reading the actual data. This
1918        parameter allows you to skip any header information present in the file before processing the
1919        data, defaults to 0
1920        :type header_len: int (optional)
1921        :param sep: The `sep` parameter in the `insert_file_to_table` function is used to specify the
1922        separator character that is used in the file being read. In this case, the default separator is
1923        set to `\t`, which represents a tab character. You can change this parameter to a different
1924        separator character if needed, defaults to \t
1925        :type sep: str (optional)
1926        :param chunksize: The `chunksize` parameter specifies the number of rows to read in at a time
1927        when processing the file in chunks. In the provided code snippet, the default value for
1928        `chunksize` is set to 1000000. This means that the file will be read in chunks of 1,, defaults
1929        to 1000000
1930        :type chunksize: int (optional)
1931        """
1932
1933        # Config
1934        chunksize = self.get_config().get("load", {}).get("chunk", chunksize)
1935        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
1936
1937        log.debug("chunksize: " + str(chunksize))
1938
1939        if chunksize:
1940            for chunk in pd.read_csv(
1941                file, skiprows=header_len, sep=sep, chunksize=chunksize, engine="c"
1942            ):
1943                if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
1944                    sql_insert_into = (
1945                        f"INSERT INTO variants ({columns}) SELECT {columns} FROM chunk"
1946                    )
1947                    #self.conn.execute(sql_insert_into)
1948                    self.get_connexion().execute(sql_insert_into)
1949                elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
1950                    chunk.to_sql("variants", self.get_connexion(), if_exists="append", index=False)
1951
1952    def load_data(
1953        self,
1954        input_file: str = None,
1955        drop_variants_table: bool = False,
1956        sample_size: int = 20480,
1957    ) -> None:
1958        """
1959        The `load_data` function reads a VCF file and inserts it into a table, with options to drop the
1960        table before loading the data and specify a sample size.
1961
1962        :param input_file: The path to the input file. This is the VCF file that will be loaded into the
1963        table
1964        :type input_file: str
1965        :param drop_variants_table: The `drop_variants_table` parameter is a boolean flag that
1966        determines whether the variants table should be dropped before loading the data. If set to
1967        `True`, the variants table will be dropped. If set to `False` (default), the variants table will
1968        not be dropped, defaults to False
1969        :type drop_variants_table: bool (optional)
1970        :param sample_size: The `sample_size` parameter determines the number of rows to be sampled from
1971        the input file. If it is set to `None`, the default value of 20480 will be used, defaults to
1972        20480
1973        :type sample_size: int (optional)
1974        """
1975
1976        log.info("Loading...")
1977
1978        # change input file
1979        if input_file:
1980            self.set_input(input_file)
1981            self.set_header()
1982
1983        # drop variants table
1984        if drop_variants_table:
1985            self.drop_variants_table()
1986
1987        # get table variants
1988        table_variants = self.get_table_variants()
1989
1990        # Access
1991        # access = self.get_config().get("access", None)
1992        access = self.get_access(default=None)
1993        log.debug(f"access: {access}")
1994
1995        # Input format and compress
1996        input_format = self.get_input_format()
1997        input_compressed = self.get_input_compressed()
1998        log.debug(f"input_format: {input_format}")
1999        log.debug(f"input_compressed: {input_compressed}")
2000
2001        # input_compressed_format
2002        if input_compressed:
2003            input_compressed_format = "gzip"
2004        else:
2005            input_compressed_format = "none"
2006        log.debug(f"input_compressed_format: {input_compressed_format}")
2007
2008        # Connexion format
2009        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
2010
2011        # Sample size
2012        if not sample_size:
2013            sample_size = -1
2014        log.debug(f"sample_size: {sample_size}")
2015
2016        # Load data
2017        log.debug(f"Load Data from {input_format}")
2018
2019        # DuckDB connexion
2020        if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
2021
2022            # Database already exists
2023            if input_format in ["db", "duckdb"]:
2024
2025                if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
2026                    log.debug(f"Input file format '{input_format}' duckDB")
2027                else:
2028                    log.error(
2029                        f"Input file format '{input_format}' not compatilbe with database format '{connexion_format}'"
2030                    )
2031                    raise ValueError(
2032                        f"Input file format '{input_format}' not compatilbe with database format '{connexion_format}'"
2033                    )
2034
2035            # Load from existing database format
2036            else:
2037
2038                try:
2039                    # Create Table or View
2040                    database = Database(database=self.input)
2041                    sql_from = database.get_sql_from(sample_size=sample_size)
2042
2043                    log.debug(f"Load Data into {table_variants}...")
2044                    if access in ["RO"]:
2045                        sql_load = (
2046                            f"CREATE VIEW {table_variants} AS SELECT * FROM {sql_from}"
2047                        )
2048                    else:
2049                        sql_load = (
2050                            f"CREATE TABLE {table_variants} AS SELECT * FROM {sql_from}"
2051                        )
2052                    self.get_connexion().execute(sql_load)
2053                    log.debug(f"Load Data into {table_variants} - done.")
2054
2055                except Exception as e:
2056                    # Format not available
2057                    msg_err = f"Load Data into {table_variants} - failed to load data: {str(e)}"
2058                    log.error(msg_err)
2059                    raise ValueError(msg_err)
2060
2061        # SQLite connexion
2062        elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"] and input_format in [
2063            "vcf",
2064            "tsv",
2065            "csv",
2066            "psv",
2067        ]:
2068
2069            # Main structure
2070            structure = {
2071                "#CHROM": "VARCHAR",
2072                "POS": "INTEGER",
2073                "ID": "VARCHAR",
2074                "REF": "VARCHAR",
2075                "ALT": "VARCHAR",
2076                "QUAL": "VARCHAR",
2077                "FILTER": "VARCHAR",
2078                "INFO": "VARCHAR",
2079            }
2080
2081            # Strcuture with samples
2082            structure_complete = structure
2083            if self.get_header_sample_list():
2084                structure["FORMAT"] = "VARCHAR"
2085                for sample in self.get_header_sample_list():
2086                    structure_complete[sample] = "VARCHAR"
2087
2088            # Columns list for create and insert
2089            sql_create_table_columns = []
2090            sql_create_table_columns_list = []
2091            for column in structure_complete:
2092                column_type = structure_complete[column]
2093                sql_create_table_columns.append(
2094                    f'"{column}" {column_type} default NULL'
2095                )
2096                sql_create_table_columns_list.append(f'"{column}"')
2097
2098            # Create database
2099            log.debug(f"Create Table {table_variants}")
2100            sql_create_table_columns_sql = ", ".join(sql_create_table_columns)
2101            sql_create_table_columns_list_sql = ", ".join(sql_create_table_columns_list)
2102            sql_create_table = f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {table_variants} ({sql_create_table_columns_sql})"
2103            self.get_connexion().execute(sql_create_table)
2104
2105            # chunksize define length of file chunk load file
2106            chunksize = 100000
2107
2108            # delimiter
2109            delimiter = file_format_delimiters.get(input_format, "\t")
2110
2111            # Load the input file
2112            with open(self.input, "rt") as input_file:
2113
2114                # Use the appropriate file handler based on the input format
2115                if input_compressed:
2116                    input_file = bgzf.open(self.input, "rt")
2117                if input_format in ["vcf"]:
2118                    header_len = self.get_header_length()
2119                else:
2120                    header_len = 0
2121
2122                # Insert the file contents into a table
2123                self.insert_file_to_table(
2124                    input_file,
2125                    columns=sql_create_table_columns_list_sql,
2126                    header_len=header_len,
2127                    sep=delimiter,
2128                    chunksize=chunksize,
2129                )
2130
2131        else:
2132            log.error(
2133                f"Connexion format '{connexion_format}' not available with format '{input_format}'"
2134            )
2135            raise ValueError(
2136                f"Connexion format '{connexion_format}' not available with format '{input_format}'"
2137            )
2138
2139        # Add INFO column if not exists
2140        if access not in ["RO"] and "INFO" not in self.get_header_columns_as_list():
2141            log.debug("INFO column not found, adding it")
2142            # Add INFO column
2143            self.add_column(
2144                table_name=table_variants,
2145                column_name="INFO",
2146                column_type="VARCHAR",
2147                default_value=None,
2148            )
2149
2150        # # Explode INFOS fields into table fields
2151        # if self.get_explode_infos():
2152        #     self.explode_infos(
2153        #         prefix=self.get_explode_infos_prefix(),
2154        #         fields=self.get_explode_infos_fields(),
2155        #         force=True,
2156        #     )
2157
2158        # Create index after insertion
2159        self.create_indexes()

2161    def get_explode_infos(self) -> bool:
2162        """
2163        The function `get_explode_infos` returns the value of the "explode_infos" parameter, defaulting
2164        to False if it is not set.
2165        :return: The method is returning the value of the "explode_infos" parameter, which is a boolean
2166        value. If the parameter is not present, it will return False.
2167        """
2168
2169        return self.get_param().get("explode", {}).get("explode_infos", False)
2170
2171    def get_explode_infos_fields(
2172        self,
2173        explode_infos_fields: str = None,
2174        remove_fields_not_in_header: bool = False,
2175    ) -> list:
2176        """
2177        The `get_explode_infos_fields` function returns a list of exploded information fields based on
2178        the input parameter `explode_infos_fields`.
2179
2180        :param explode_infos_fields: The `explode_infos_fields` parameter is a string that specifies the
2181        fields to be exploded. It can be set to "ALL" to explode all fields, or it can be a
2182        comma-separated list of field names to explode
2183        :type explode_infos_fields: str
2184        :param remove_fields_not_in_header: The parameter `remove_fields_not_in_header` is a boolean
2185        flag that determines whether to remove fields that are not present in the header. If it is set
2186        to `True`, any field that is not in the header will be excluded from the list of exploded
2187        information fields. If it is set to `, defaults to False
2188        :type remove_fields_not_in_header: bool (optional)
2189        :return: The function `get_explode_infos_fields` returns a list of exploded information fields.
2190        If the `explode_infos_fields` parameter is not provided or is set to None, it returns an empty
2191        list. If the parameter is provided and its value is "ALL", it also returns an empty list.
2192        Otherwise, it returns a list of exploded information fields after removing any spaces and
2193        splitting the string by commas.
2194        """
2195
2196        # If no fields, get it in param
2197        if not explode_infos_fields:
2198            explode_infos_fields = (
2199                self.get_param().get("explode", {}).get("explode_infos_fields", None)
2200            )
2201
2202        # If no fields, defined as all fields in header using keyword
2203        if not explode_infos_fields:
2204            explode_infos_fields = "*"
2205
2206        # If fields list not empty
2207        if explode_infos_fields:
2208
2209            # Input fields list
2210            if isinstance(explode_infos_fields, str):
2211                fields_input = explode_infos_fields.split(",")
2212            elif isinstance(explode_infos_fields, list):
2213                fields_input = explode_infos_fields
2214            else:
2215                fields_input = []
2216
2217            # Fields list without * keyword
2218            fields_without_all = fields_input.copy()
2219            if "*".casefold() in (item.casefold() for item in fields_without_all):
2220                fields_without_all.remove("*")
2221
2222            # Fields in header
2223            fields_in_header = sorted(list(set(self.get_header().infos)))
2224
2225            # Construct list of fields
2226            fields_output = []
2227            for field in fields_input:
2228
2229                # Strip field
2230                field = field.strip()
2231
2232                # format keyword * in regex
2233                if field.upper() in ["*"]:
2234                    field = ".*"
2235
2236                # Find all fields with pattern
2237                # Check if field is in header (to prevent special caracters in field such as '+', e.g. 'GERP++_RS')
2238                if field in fields_in_header:
2239                    fields_search = [field]
2240                else:
2241                    r = re.compile(rf"^{field}$")
2242                    fields_search = sorted(list(filter(r.match, fields_in_header)))
2243
2244                # Remove fields input from search
2245                if field in fields_search:
2246                    fields_search = [field]
2247                elif fields_search != [field]:
2248                    fields_search = sorted(
2249                        list(set(fields_search).difference(fields_input))
2250                    )
2251
2252                # If field is not in header (avoid not well formatted header)
2253                if not fields_search and not remove_fields_not_in_header:
2254                    fields_search = [field]
2255
2256                # Add found fields
2257                for new_field in fields_search:
2258                    # Add field, if not already exists, and if it is in header (if asked)
2259                    if (
2260                        new_field not in fields_output
2261                        and (
2262                            not remove_fields_not_in_header
2263                            or new_field in fields_in_header
2264                        )
2265                        and new_field not in [".*"]
2266                    ):
2267                        fields_output.append(new_field)
2268
2269            return fields_output
2270
2271        else:
2272
2273            return []
2274
2275    def get_explode_infos_prefix(self, explode_infos_prefix: str = None) -> str:
2276        """
2277        The function `get_explode_infos_prefix` returns the value of the `explode_infos_prefix` parameter, or
2278        the value of `self.get_param().get("explode_infos_prefix", None)` if `explode_infos_prefix` is

2282        prefix to be used for exploding or expanding information

2287        if not explode_infos_prefix:
2288            explode_infos_prefix = (
2289                self.get_param().get("explode", {}).get("explode_infos_prefix", "")
2290            )

2292        return explode_infos_prefix
