4989    ##############################
4990    # Function format annotation #
4991    ##############################
4992
4993    def annotation_format_to_table(
4994        self,
4995        annotation_field: str = "ANN",
4996        annotation_id: str = "Feature_ID",
4997        view_name: str = "transcripts",
4998        view_type: str = "view",
4999        column_rename: dict = {},
5000        column_clean: bool = False,
5001        column_case: str = None,
5002        column_split: str = "&",
5003    ) -> str:
5004        """
5005        Converts annotation data from a VCF file into a structured table format, ensuring unique values
5006        and creating a temporary table for further processing or analysis.
5007
5008        Args:
5009            annotation_field (str, optional): The field in the VCF file that contains the annotation information
5010                for each variant. Defaults to "ANN".
5011            annotation_id (str, optional): The identifier for the annotation feature, used as a column name
5012                in the resulting table or view. Defaults to "Feature_ID".
5013            view_name (str, optional): The name of the temporary table that will be created to store the transformed
5014                annotation data. Defaults to "transcripts".
5015            view_type (str, optional): The type of the view to be created. Defaults to "view".
5016            column_rename (dict, optional): A dictionary to specify custom renaming for columns. By providing key-value
5017                pairs in this dictionary, you can rename specific columns in the resulting table or view.
5018            column_clean (bool, optional): A flag to determine whether the annotation field should undergo a cleaning process.
5019                If set to True, the function will clean the annotation field before further processing. Defaults to False.
5020            column_case (str, optional): Specifies the case transformation to be applied to the column names extracted from
5021                the annotation data. It allows you to set the case of the column names to either lowercase or uppercase.
5022            column_split (str, optional): The separator to split field values. Defaults to "&". Set to None to disable splitting.
5023
5024        Returns:
5025            str: The name of the view created, which is stored in the variable `view_name`.
5026        """
5027
5028        # annotation_id original name
5029        annotation_id_original = annotation_id
5030
5031        # Transcript annotation
5032        if column_rename:
5033            annotation_id = column_rename.get(annotation_id, annotation_id)
5034
5035        if column_clean:
5036            annotation_id = clean_annotation_field(annotation_id)
5037
5038        # Prefix
5039        prefix = self.get_explode_infos_prefix()
5040        if prefix:
5041            prefix = "INFO/"
5042
5043        # Variants table
5044        table_variants = self.get_table_variants()
5045
5046        # Header
5047        vcf_reader = self.get_header()
5048
5049        # Add columns
5050        added_columns = []
5051        added_columns_type = {}
5052
5053        # If annotation_field exists
5054        if annotation_field in vcf_reader.infos:
5055
5056            # Extract ANN header
5057            ann_description = vcf_reader.infos[annotation_field].desc
5058            pattern = r"'(.+?)'"
5059            match = re.search(pattern, ann_description)
5060            if match:
5061                ann_header_match = match.group(1).split(" | ")
5062                ann_header = []
5063                ann_header_desc = {}
5064                for i in range(len(ann_header_match)):
5065                    ann_header_info = "".join(
5066                        char for char in ann_header_match[i] if char.isalnum()
5067                    )
5068                    ann_header.append(ann_header_info)
5069                    ann_header_desc[ann_header_info] = ann_header_match[i]
5070                if not ann_header_desc:
5071                    raise ValueError("Invalid header description format")
5072            else:
5073                raise ValueError("Invalid header description format")
5074
5075            # annotation field pattern
5076            annotation_field_pattern = rf"(^|;)({annotation_field})=([^;]*)?"
5077
5078            annotation_fields_for_format = []
5079            for i, header in enumerate(ann_header_desc.values()):
5080                if header in [annotation_id_original]:
5081                    annotation_fields_for_format.append(
5082                        f"SPLIT_PART(annotation, '|', {i+1}) AS '{header}'"
5083                    )
5084                else:
5085                    annotation_fields_for_format.append(
5086                        f"string_agg(SPLIT_PART(annotation, '|', {i+1}), ',') AS '{header}'"
5087                    )
5088
5089            query = f""" 
5090                WITH exploded_annotations AS (
5091                    SELECT
5092                        "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,
5093                        UNNEST(
5094                            STRING_SPLIT(
5095                                regexp_extract("INFO", '{annotation_field_pattern}', 3),
5096                                ','
5097                            )
5098                        ) AS annotation
5099                    FROM {table_variants}
5100                ),
5101                split_annotations AS (
5102                    SELECT
5103                        "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,
5104                        {", ".join(annotation_fields_for_format)}
5105                    FROM exploded_annotations
5106                    GROUP BY "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT, "{annotation_id_original}"
5107                )
5108                SELECT * FROM split_annotations
5109                LIMIT 10000
5110                """
5111            dataframe_annotation_format = self.get_query_to_df(query=query)
5112
5113            # Init
5114            query_list_keys = []
5115            key_i = 0
5116
5117            for key in dataframe_annotation_format.keys():
5118
5119                if key in ann_header_desc.values():
5120
5121                    # Key
5122                    key_i += 1
5123                    key_clean = key
5124
5125                    # key rename
5126                    if column_rename:
5127                        key_clean = column_rename.get(key_clean, key_clean)
5128
5129                    # key clean
5130                    if column_clean:
5131                        key_clean = clean_annotation_field(key_clean)
5132
5133                    # Key case
5134                    if column_case:
5135                        if column_case.lower() in ["lower"]:
5136                            key_clean = key_clean.lower()
5137                        elif column_case.lower() in ["upper"]:
5138                            key_clean = key_clean.upper()
5139
5140                    # Detect column type
5141                    column_type = detect_column_type(dataframe_annotation_format[key])
5142                    added_columns_type[key] = column_type
5143                    log.debug(f"Field '{key}' type detected: {column_type}")
5144
5145                    # Append key to list
5146                    if column_split is not None:
5147                        query_list_keys.append(
5148                            f""" TRY_CAST(replace(NULLIF(SPLIT_PART(annotation, '|', {key_i}), ''), '{column_split}', ',') AS {column_type}) AS '{prefix}{key_clean}' """
5149                        )
5150                    else:
5151                        query_list_keys.append(
5152                            f""" TRY_CAST(NULLIF(SPLIT_PART(annotation, '|', {key_i}), '') AS {column_type}) AS '{prefix}{key_clean}' """
5153                        )
5154
5155            # Create temporary table
5156            query_create_view = f"""
5157                CREATE {view_type} {view_name} AS (
5158                    WITH exploded_annotations AS (
5159                        SELECT
5160                            "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,
5161                            UNNEST(
5162                                STRING_SPLIT(
5163                                    regexp_extract("INFO", '{annotation_field_pattern}', 3),
5164                                    ','
5165                                )
5166                            ) AS annotation
5167                        FROM {table_variants}
5168                    ),
5169                    split_annotations AS (
5170                        SELECT
5171                            "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,
5172                            {", ".join(query_list_keys)},
5173                        FROM exploded_annotations
5174                    )
5175                    SELECT *, {annotation_id} AS 'transcript' FROM split_annotations
5176                )
5177            """
5178            # log.debug(f"Create view FORMAT:{query_create_view}")
5179            self.execute_query(query=query_create_view)
5180
5181        else:
5182
5183            # Return None
5184            view_name = None
5185
5186        return view_name, added_columns, added_columns_type
5187
5188    ############################
5189    # Rename and remove fields #
5190    ############################
5191
5192    def rename_info_fields(
5193        self, fields_to_rename: dict = None, table: str = None
5194    ) -> dict:
5195        """
5196        The `rename_info_fields` function renames specified fields in a VCF file header and updates
5197        corresponding INFO fields in the variants table.
5198
5199        :param fields_to_rename: The `fields_to_rename` parameter is a dictionary that contains the
5200        mapping of fields to be renamed in a VCF (Variant Call Format) file. The keys in the dictionary
5201        represent the original field names that need to be renamed, and the corresponding values
5202        represent the new names to which the fields should be
5203        :type fields_to_rename: dict
5204        :param table: The `table` parameter in the `rename_info_fields` function represents the name of
5205        the table in which the variants data is stored. This table contains information about genetic
5206        variants, and the function updates the corresponding INFO fields in this table when renaming
5207        specified fields in the VCF file header
5208        :type table: str
5209        :return: The `rename_info_fields` function returns a dictionary `fields_processed` that contains
5210        the original field names as keys and their corresponding new names (or None if the field was
5211        removed) as values after renaming or removing specified fields in a VCF file header and updating
5212        corresponding INFO fields in the variants table.
5213        """
5214
5215        # Config
5216        config = self.get_config()
5217
5218        # Access
5219        # access = config.get("access")
5220        access = self.get_access(default=None)
5221
5222        # Init
5223        fields_processed = {
5224            "renamed": {},
5225            "removed": {},
5226            "not_processed": {},
5227            "not_found": {},
5228        }
5229
5230        if table is None:
5231            table = self.get_table_variants()
5232
5233        # Clasue case
5234        clause_case = []
5235
5236        # Init
5237        fields_to_process = {}
5238
5239        # For each field to rename or remove, one by one
5240        if fields_to_rename is not None:
5241            for field_to_rename, field_renamed in fields_to_rename.items():
5242
5243                # If no field to process
5244                if field_to_rename != "":
5245
5246                    # rename empty is remove
5247                    if field_renamed == "":
5248                        field_renamed = None
5249
5250                    # Check if already to process
5251                    check_field_to_rename_found = False
5252                    for (
5253                        field_to_process_to_rename,
5254                        field_to_process_renamed,
5255                    ) in fields_to_process.items():
5256                        if field_to_rename == field_to_process_renamed:
5257                            # Replace filed to process
5258                            fields_to_process[field_to_process_to_rename] = (
5259                                field_renamed
5260                            )
5261                            check_field_to_rename_found = True
5262                    if not check_field_to_rename_found:
5263                        # Add field to process
5264                        fields_to_process[field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5265
5266        if len(fields_to_process) and access not in ["RO"]:
5267
5268            # Log
5269            log.info("Rename or remove fields...")
5270
5271            # Header
5272            header = self.get_header()
5273
5274            # For each field
5275            for field_to_rename, field_renamed in fields_to_process.items():
5276
5277                # If to rename or remove
5278                if (
5279                    field_to_rename != field_renamed
5280                    and field_to_rename not in ["", None]
5281                    and field_renamed not in [""]
5282                ):
5283
5284                    # Rename
5285                    if field_renamed is not None:
5286
5287                        # Case clause
5288                        clause_case.append(
5289                            f""" WHEN k = '{field_to_rename}' THEN '{field_renamed}'  """
5290                        )
5291
5292                        # Fields processed
5293                        fields_processed["renamed"][field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5294
5295                        # Log
5296                        log.debug(
5297                            f"Rename or remove fields - field '{field_to_rename}' renamed as '{field_renamed}'"
5298                        )
5299
5300                    # Remove
5301                    else:
5302
5303                        # Case clause
5304                        clause_case.append(
5305                            f""" WHEN k = '{field_to_rename}' THEN NULL  """
5306                        )
5307
5308                        # Fields processed
5309                        fields_processed["removed"][field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5310
5311                        # Log
5312                        log.debug(
5313                            f"Rename or remove fields - field '{field_to_rename}' removed"
5314                        )
5315
5316                    # Header
5317                    if field_to_rename in header.infos:
5318
5319                        # Rename header if to rename
5320                        if field_renamed is not None:
5321                            header.infos[field_renamed] = vcf.parser._Info(
5322                                field_renamed,
5323                                header.infos[field_to_rename].num,
5324                                header.infos[field_to_rename].type,
5325                                header.infos[field_to_rename].desc,
5326                                header.infos[field_to_rename].source,
5327                                header.infos[field_to_rename].version,
5328                                header.infos[field_to_rename].type_code,
5329                            )
5330
5331                        # Remove header, if rename or remove
5332                        del header.infos[field_to_rename]
5333
5334                    else:
5335
5336                        # Log
5337                        log.warning(
5338                            f"Rename or remove fields - field '{field_to_rename}' not in header"
5339                        )
5340
5341                        # Fields processed
5342                        fields_processed["not_found"][field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5343
5344                else:
5345
5346                    # Fields processed
5347                    fields_processed["not_pocessed"][field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5348
5349            # Process
5350            if len(clause_case):
5351
5352                # Update query
5353                query_update = f"""
5354                    UPDATE {table}
5355                    SET INFO = renamed_table.INFO                       -- update INFO
5356                    FROM (
5357                        SELECT
5358                            "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,                    -- variant id
5359                            IFNULL(string_agg(kv, ';'), '.') AS INFO    -- INFO
5360                        FROM (
5361                            SELECT
5362                                "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,                -- variant id
5363                                CASE
5364                                    WHEN k IS NOT NULL                  -- key not null
5365                                    THEN
5366                                        CASE 
5367                                            WHEN v IS NOT NULL          -- value not null
5368                                            THEN concat(k, '=', v)      -- key-value: either String, Integer, Float
5369                                            ELSE k                      -- Flag
5370                                        END
5371                                    ELSE NULL                           -- remove
5372                                END AS kv
5373                            FROM (
5374                                SELECT "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,         -- variant id
5375                                    CASE
5376                                        {" ".join(clause_case)}         -- rename or remove
5377                                        ELSE k                          -- no change
5378                                    END AS k,                           -- key
5379                                    v                                   -- value
5380                                FROM (
5381                                    SELECT
5382                                        "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,        -- variant id
5383                                        string_split(kv, '=')[1] AS k,  -- key
5384                                        string_split(kv, '=')[2] AS v   -- value
5385                                    FROM (
5386                                        SELECT "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT, unnest(string_split(INFO, ';')) AS kv
5387                                        FROM variants
5388                                        )
5389                                    )
5390                                )
5391                            )
5392                        GROUP BY "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT
5393                    ) AS renamed_table
5394                    WHERE {table}."#CHROM" = renamed_table."#CHROM"     -- join
5395                    AND {table}."POS" = renamed_table."POS"
5396                    AND {table}."REF" = renamed_table."REF"
5397                    AND {table}."ALT" = renamed_table."ALT"
5398                """
5399                # log.debug(f"query_update={query_update}")
5400                self.execute_query(query_update)
5401
5402        return fields_processed
5403
5404    def recreate_info_fields(
5405        self, fields_to_rename: dict = None, table: str = None
5406    ) -> dict:
5407        """
5408        The `recreate_info_fields` function renames specified fields in a VCF file header and updates
5409        corresponding INFO fields in the variants table.
5410
5411        :param fields_to_rename: The `fields_to_rename` parameter is a dictionary that contains the
5412        mapping of fields to be renamed in a VCF (Variant Call Format) file. The keys in the dictionary
5413        represent the original field names that need to be renamed, and the corresponding values
5414        represent the new names to which the fields should be renamed. Default {}
5415        :type fields_to_rename: dict
5416        :param table: The `table` parameter in the `recreate_info_fields` function represents the name of
5417        the table in which the variants data is stored. This table contains information about genetic
5418        variants, and the function updates the corresponding INFO fields in this table when renaming
5419        specified fields in the VCF file header. Default Variants table 'variants'.
5420        :type table: str
5421        :return: The `recreate_info_fields` function returns a dictionary `fields_renamed` that contains
5422        the original field names as keys and their corresponding new names (or None if the field was
5423        removed) as values after renaming or removing specified fields in a VCF file header and updating
5424        corresponding INFO fields in the variants table.
5425        """
5426
5427        # Init
5428        config = self.get_config()
5429
5430        # Access
5431        # access = config.get("access")
5432        access = self.get_access(default=None)
5433
5434        # Table
5435        if table is None:
5436            table = self.get_table_variants()
5437
5438        # Fields to rename or remove
5439        if fields_to_rename is None:
5440            fields_to_rename = {}
5441
5442        # Fields on header
5443        fields_to_process = {k: k for k in self.get_header().infos.keys()}
5444
5445        # For each field to rename or remove, one by one
5446        for field_to_rename, field_renamed in fields_to_rename.items():
5447            log.debug(f"{field_to_rename}, {field_renamed}")
5448            if field_to_rename != "" and field_renamed != "":
5449                log.debug(f"{field_to_rename}, {field_renamed} OK")
5450                # Check if already to process
5451                check_field_to_rename_found = False
5452                for (
5453                    field_to_process_to_rename,
5454                    field_to_process_renamed,
5455                ) in fields_to_process.items():
5456                    if field_to_rename == field_to_process_renamed:
5457                        fields_to_process[field_to_process_to_rename] = field_renamed
5458                        check_field_to_rename_found = True
5459                if not check_field_to_rename_found:
5460                    fields_to_process[field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5461
5462        # Init
5463        fields_processed = {"removed": {}, "renamed": {}, "not_found": {}}
5464
5465        # if fields_to_rename is not None and access not in ["RO"]:
5466        if fields_to_process is not None and access not in ["RO"]:
5467
5468            log.info(f"Recreate INFO with {len(fields_to_process)} fields...")
5469
5470            # Create view
5471            annotation_view_name = "annotation_view_for_recreate_infos_" + str(
5472                get_random()
5473            )
5474
5475            # Header
5476            header = self.get_header()
5477
5478            # Update query select clauses
5479            query_view_select_clause = []
5480
5481            for field_to_rename, field_renamed in fields_to_process.items():
5482
5483                # Action
5484                action = None
5485
5486                # Header
5487
5488                # Field to remove
5489                if field_renamed is None:
5490
5491                    if field_renamed in header.infos:
5492
5493                        # Remove in header
5494                        del header.infos[field_renamed]
5495
5496                    # Action
5497                    action = "removed"
5498
5499                # Field to rename
5500                elif field_to_rename in header.infos:
5501
5502                    # Rename header
5503                    if field_renamed is not None and field_renamed != field_to_rename:
5504                        header.infos[field_renamed] = vcf.parser._Info(
5505                            field_renamed,
5506                            header.infos[field_to_rename].num,
5507                            header.infos[field_to_rename].type,
5508                            header.infos[field_to_rename].desc,
5509                            header.infos[field_to_rename].source,
5510                            header.infos[field_to_rename].version,
5511                            header.infos[field_to_rename].type_code,
5512                        )
5513                        del header.infos[field_to_rename]
5514
5515                    # Update query
5516                    if header.infos[field_renamed].type == "Flag":
5517                        query_view_select_clause.append(
5518                            f"""
5519                                CASE
5520                                    WHEN "{field_renamed}" IS NOT NULL AND TRY_CAST("{field_renamed}" AS FLOAT) != 0
5521                                    THEN '{field_renamed};'
5522                                END
5523                            """
5524                        )
5525                    else:
5526                        query_view_select_clause.append(
5527                            f"""
5528                                CASE
5529                                    WHEN "{field_renamed}" IS NOT NULL
5530                                    THEN concat('{field_renamed}=',"{field_renamed}",';')
5531                                END
5532                            """
5533                        )
5534
5535                    # Action
5536                    action = "renamed"
5537
5538                else:
5539
5540                    log.warning(
5541                        f"Rename or remove fields - field '{field_to_rename}' not in header"
5542                    )
5543
5544                    # Action
5545                    action = "not_found"
5546
5547                # List of renamed or removed fields
5548                if action:
5549                    fields_processed[action][field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5550
5551            if len(query_view_select_clause):
5552
5553                # Create view
5554                annotation_view_name = self.create_annotations_view(
5555                    table=table,
5556                    view=annotation_view_name,
5557                    view_type="view",
5558                    view_mode="full",
5559                    info_prefix_column="",
5560                    # info_struct_column="INFOS",
5561                    detect_type_list=False,
5562                    fields=fields_processed["renamed"].keys(),
5563                    fields_not_exists=True,
5564                    fields_forced_as_varchar=True,
5565                    fields_needed_all=False,
5566                    fields_to_rename=fields_processed["renamed"],
5567                    drop_view=True,
5568                )
5569
5570                # Log
5571                log.info(
5572                    f"Recreate INFO with {len(query_view_select_clause)} found fields..."
5573                )
5574
5575                # Query
5576                query = f"""
5577                    UPDATE {table}
5578                    SET
5579                        INFO = regexp_replace(
5580                                concat({", ".join(query_view_select_clause)}),
5581                                ';$',
5582                                ''
5583                            )
5584                    FROM {annotation_view_name}
5585                    WHERE {table}."#CHROM" = {annotation_view_name}."#CHROM"
5586                      AND {table}."POS" = {annotation_view_name}."POS"
5587                      AND {table}."REF" = {annotation_view_name}."REF"
5588                      AND {table}."ALT" = {annotation_view_name}."ALT"
5589                """
5590                # log.debug(f"query={query}")
5591
5592                # Excecute query
5593                self.execute_query(query=query)
5594
5595        return fields_processed
5596
5597    def calculation_rename_info_fields(
5598        self,
5599        fields_to_rename: dict = None,
5600        table: str = None,
5601        operation_name: str = "RENAME_INFO_FIELDS",
5602    ) -> None:
5603        """
5604        The `calculation_rename_info_fields` function retrieves parameters from a dictionary, updates
5605        fields to rename and table if provided, and then calls another function to rename the fields.
5606
5607        :param fields_to_rename: `fields_to_rename` is a dictionary that contains the fields to be
5608        renamed in a table. Each key-value pair in the dictionary represents the original field name as
5609        the key and the new field name as the value
5610        :type fields_to_rename: dict

def load_header( self, header=None, table: str = None, drop: bool = False, view_name: str = 'header') -> str: 
151    def load_header(
152        self,
153        header=None,
154        table: str = None,
155        drop: bool = False,
156        view_name: str = "header",
157    ) -> str:
158        """
159        Load header in a table, with INFO, FORMAT, FILTERS, SAMPLES and METADATA
160
161        Args:
162            header (vcfobject, optional): VCF object from pyVCF. Defaults to None (header of the Variants object).
163            table (str, optional): Table name of the header table. Defaults to None (defined as 'header' later).
164            drop (bool, optional): Drop table if exists. Defaults to False.
165            view_name (str, optional): Name of the table. Defaults to 'header'.
166
167        Returns:
168            str: Name of the table, None otherwise
169
170        """
171
172        def create_header_table(conn):
173            """
174            Create header table
175
176            Args:
177                conn (conn): Database connexion.
178
179            """
180
181            # Columns
182            columns = [
183                "section VARCHAR",
184                "id VARCHAR",
185                "number VARCHAR",
186                "type VARCHAR",
187                "description VARCHAR",
188            ]
189
190            # Query create
191            query_create = f"""
192            CREATE OR REPLACE table {view_name} (
193                {', '.join(columns)},
194                PRIMARY KEY (section, id)
195            );
196            """
197
198            # Execute
199            conn.execute(query_create)
200
201        def insert_header(conn, vcf_header):
202            """
203            Insert header into table
204
205            Args:
206                conn (conn): Database connexion.
207
208            """
209
210            # Init
211            inserts = []
212
213            # Add INFO section
214            for info_id, info in vcf_header.infos.items():
215                inserts.append(
216                    (
217                        "INFO",
218                        info_id,
219                        str(info.num if info.num is not None else "."),
220                        info.type if info.type is not None else "",
221                        info.desc if info.desc is not None else "",
222                    )
223                )
224
225            # Add FORMAT section
226            for format_id, format in vcf_header.formats.items():
227                inserts.append(
228                    (
229                        "FORMAT",
230                        format_id,
231                        str(format.num if format.num is not None else "."),
232                        format.type if format.type is not None else "",
233                        format.desc if format.desc is not None else "",
234                    )
235                )
236
237            # Add FILTER section
238            for filter_id, filter in vcf_header.filters.items():
239                inserts.append(
240                    (
241                        "FILTER",
242                        filter_id,
243                        "",
244                        "",
245                        filter.desc if filter.desc is not None else "",
246                    )
247                )
248
249            # Add Samples
250            for sample_id in vcf_header.samples:
251                inserts.append(
252                    (
253                        "SAMPLE",
254                        sample_id,
255                        "",
256                        "",
257                        "",
258                    )
259                )
260
261            # Add Metadata
262            for key, value in vcf_header.metadata.items():
263                inserts.append(
264                    (
265                        "METADATA",
266                        key,
267                        "",
268                        "",
269                        str(value) if value is not None else "",
270                    )
271                )
272
273            # Create query of insert with parameters
274            query_insert = f"""
275            INSERT INTO {view_name} (section, id, number, type, description) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?);
276            """
277            conn.executemany(query_insert, inserts)
278
279        # Get header is None
280        if header is None:
281            header = self.get_header()
282
283        # Header table
284        if table is None:
285            table = "header"
286
287        # If header is not None
288        if header is not None:
289
290            # Connexion
291            conn = self.get_connexion()
292
293            # Drop table
294            if drop:
295                query_drop = f"""
296                DROP TABLE IF EXISTS {table}
297                """
298                conn.execute(query_drop)
299
300            # Create table
301            create_header_table(conn)
302            insert_header(conn, header)
303
304            return table
305
306        else:
307
308            return None

Load header in a table, with INFO, FORMAT, FILTERS, SAMPLES and METADATA

Args: header (vcfobject, optional): VCF object from pyVCF. Defaults to None (header of the Variants object). table (str, optional): Table name of the header table. Defaults to None (defined as 'header' later). drop (bool, optional): Drop table if exists. Defaults to False. view_name (str, optional): Name of the table. Defaults to 'header'.

Returns: str: Name of the table, None otherwise

def get_connexion_config(self) -> dict: 
432    def get_connexion_config(self) -> dict:
433        """
434        The function `get_connexion_config` returns a dictionary containing the configuration for a
435        connection, including the number of threads and memory limit.
436        :return: a dictionary containing the configuration for the Connexion library.
437        """
438
439        # config
440        config = self.get_config()
441
442        # Connexion config
443        connexion_config = {}
444        threads = self.get_threads()
445
446        # Threads
447        if threads:
448            connexion_config["threads"] = threads
449
450        # Memory
451        # if config.get("memory", None):
452        #     connexion_config["memory_limit"] = config.get("memory")
453        if self.get_memory():
454            connexion_config["memory_limit"] = self.get_memory()
455
456        # Temporary directory
457        if config.get("temp_directory", None):
458            connexion_config["temp_directory"] = config.get("temp_directory")
459        else:
460            config["temp_directory"] = os.path.join(
461                self.get_tmp_dir(), f"duckdb_temp_" + get_random(10)
462            )
463            self.set_config(config)
464            connexion_config["temp_directory"] = config["temp_directory"]
465
466        # Access
467        access = self.get_access(default=None)
468        if access:
469            access_mode = access
470            if access in ["RO"]:
471                access_mode = "READ_ONLY"
472            elif access in ["RW"]:
473                access_mode = "READ_WRITE"
474            connexion_db = self.get_connexion_db()
475            if connexion_db in ":memory:":
476                access_mode = "READ_WRITE"
477            connexion_config["access_mode"] = access_mode
478
479        return connexion_config

The function get_connexion_config returns a dictionary containing the configuration for a connection, including the number of threads and memory limit.

Returns

a dictionary containing the configuration for the Connexion library.

533    def set_connexion(self, conn) -> None:
534        """
535        The function `set_connexion` creates a connection to a database, with options for different
536        database formats and settings.
537
538        :param conn: The `conn` parameter in the `set_connexion` method is the connection to the
539        database. If a connection is not provided, a new connection to an in-memory database is created.
540        The method then proceeds to set up the connection based on the specified format (e.g., duckdb or
541        sqlite
542        """
543
544        # Connexion db
545        connexion_db = self.set_connexion_db()
546
547        # Connexion config
548        connexion_config = self.get_connexion_config()
549
550        # Connexion format
551        connexion_format = self.get_config().get("connexion_format", "duckdb")
552        # Set connexion format
553        self.connexion_format = connexion_format
554
555        # Connexion
556        if not conn:
557            if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
558                conn = duckdb.connect(connexion_db, config=connexion_config)
559                # duckDB settings
560                duckdb_settings = self.get_duckdb_settings()
561                if duckdb_settings:
562                    for setting in duckdb_settings:
563                        setting_value = duckdb_settings.get(setting)
564                        if isinstance(setting_value, str):
565                            setting_value = f"'{setting_value}'"
566                        conn.execute(f"PRAGMA {setting}={setting_value};")
567                # duckDB settings arrow large buffer size
568                conn.execute("SET arrow_large_buffer_size=true")
569                # settings = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM duckdb_settings()").df()
570                # log.debug(f"DuckDB settings after connexion:\n{settings.to_string()}")
571            elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
572                conn = sqlite3.connect(connexion_db)
573
574        # Set connexion
575        self.conn = conn
576
577        # Log
578        log.debug(f"connexion_format: {connexion_format}")
579        log.debug(f"connexion_db: {connexion_db}")
580        log.debug(f"connexion config: {connexion_config}")
581        log.debug(f"connexion duckdb settings: {self.get_duckdb_settings()}")
582        log.debug("connexion duckdb settings: arrow_large_buffer_size=true")

585        """
586        The `set_output` function in Python sets the output file based on the input or a specified key
587        in the config file, extracting the output name, extension, and format.
588
589        :param output: The `output` parameter in the `set_output` method is used to specify the name of
590        the output file. If the config file has an 'output' key, the method sets the output to the value
591        of that key. If no output is provided, it sets the output to `None`
592        :type output: str
593        """
594
595        if output and not isinstance(output, str):
596            self.output = output.name
597        else:
598            self.output = output
599
600        # Output format
601        if self.output:
602            output_name, output_extension = os.path.splitext(self.output)
603            self.output_name = output_name
604            self.output_extension = output_extension
605            self.output_format = self.output_extension.replace(".", "")
606        else:
607            self.output_name = None
608            self.output_extension = None
609            self.output_format = None

def set_header(self) -> None: 
611    def set_header(self) -> None:
612        """
613        It reads the header of a VCF file and stores it as a list of strings and as a VCF object
614        """
615
616        input_file = self.get_input()
617        default_header_list = [
618            "##fileformat=VCFv4.2",
619            "#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT	QUAL	FILTER	INFO",
620        ]
621
622        # Full path
623        input_file = full_path(input_file)
624
625        if input_file:
626
627            input_format = self.get_input_format()
628            input_compressed = self.get_input_compressed()
629            config = self.get_config()
630            header_list = default_header_list
631            if input_format in [
632                "vcf",
633                "hdr",
634                "tsv",
635                "csv",
636                "psv",
637                "parquet",
638                "db",
639                "duckdb",
640                "json",
641            ]:
642                # header provided in param
643                if config.get("header_file", None):
644                    with open(config.get("header_file"), "rt") as f:
645                        header_list = self.read_vcf_header(f)
646                # within a vcf file format (header within input file itsself)
647                elif input_format in ["vcf", "hdr"] and not os.path.isdir(input_file):
648                    # within a compressed vcf file format (.vcf.gz)
649                    if input_compressed:
650                        with bgzf.open(input_file, "rt") as f:
651                            header_list = self.read_vcf_header(f)
652                    # within an uncompressed vcf file format (.vcf)
653                    else:
654                        with open(input_file, "rt") as f:
655                            header_list = self.read_vcf_header(f)
656                # header provided in default external file .hdr
657                elif os.path.exists((input_file + ".hdr")):
658                    with open(input_file + ".hdr", "rt") as f:
659                        header_list = self.read_vcf_header(f)
660                else:
661                    try:  # Try to get header info fields and file columns
662
663                        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
664
665                            # Create database
666                            db_for_header = Database(database=input_file)
667
668                            # Get header columns for infos fields
669                            db_header_from_columns = (
670                                db_for_header.get_header_from_columns()
671                            )
672
673                            # Get real columns in the file
674                            db_header_columns = db_for_header.get_columns()
675
676                            # Write header file
677                            header_file_tmp = os.path.join(tmpdir, "header")
678                            f = open(header_file_tmp, "w")
679                            vcf.Writer(f, db_header_from_columns)
680                            f.close()
681
682                            # Replace #CHROM line with rel columns
683                            header_list = db_for_header.read_header_file(
684                                header_file=header_file_tmp
685                            )
686                            header_list[-1] = "\t".join(db_header_columns)
687
688                    except:
689
690                        log.warning(
691                            f"No header for file {input_file}. Set as default VCF header"
692                        )
693                        header_list = default_header_list
694
695            else:  # try for unknown format ?
696
697                log.error(f"Input file format '{input_format}' not available")
698                raise ValueError(f"Input file format '{input_format}' not available")
699
700            if not header_list:
701                header_list = default_header_list
702
703            # header as list
704            self.header_list = header_list
705
706            # header as VCF object
707            self.header_vcf = vcf.Reader(io.StringIO("\n".join(header_list)))
708
709        else:
710
711            self.header_list = None
712            self.header_vcf = None

def get_query_to_df(self, query: str = '', limit: int = None) -> pandas.core.frame.DataFrame: 
714    def get_query_to_df(self, query: str = "", limit: int = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
715        """
716        The `get_query_to_df` function takes a query as a string and returns the result as a pandas
717        DataFrame based on the connection format. It supports both limited and full queries.
718
719        :param query: The `query` parameter in the `get_query_to_df` function is a string that
720        represents the SQL query you want to execute. This query will be used to fetch data from a
721        database and convert it into a pandas DataFrame
722        :type query: str
723        :param limit: The `limit` parameter in the `get_query_to_df` function is used to specify the
724        maximum number of rows to be returned in the resulting dataframe. If a limit is provided, the
725        function will only fetch up to that number of rows from the database query result. If no limit
726        is specified,
727        :type limit: int
728        :return: A pandas DataFrame is being returned by the `get_query_to_df` function.
729        """
730
731        # Connexion format
732        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
733
734        # Limit in query
735        if limit:
736
737            # Panda settings
738            pd.set_option("display.max_rows", limit)
739
740            # DuckDB connexion
741            if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
742
743                result = self.get_connexion().execute(query).fetch_record_batch(limit)
744                if result is None:
745                    df = result.df()
746                else:
747                    try:
748                        df = result.read_next_batch().to_pandas()
749                    except StopIteration:
750                        df = self.get_connexion().execute(query).df()[0:limit]
751
752            # SQLite connexion
753            elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
754                df = next(pd.read_sql_query(query, self.conn, chunksize=limit))
755
756        # Full query without limit
757        else:
758
759            # DuckDB connexion
760            if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
761                df = self.get_connexion().execute(query).df()
762
763            # SQLite connexion
764            elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
765                df = pd.read_sql_query(query, self.conn)
766
767        return df

The get_query_to_df function takes a query as a string and returns the result as a pandas DataFrame based on the connection format. It supports both limited and full queries.

Parameters
  • query: The query parameter in the get_query_to_df function is a string that represents the SQL query you want to execute. This query will be used to fetch data from a database and convert it into a pandas DataFrame
  • limit: The limit parameter in the get_query_to_df function is used to specify the maximum number of rows to be returned in the resulting dataframe. If a limit is provided, the function will only fetch up to that number of rows from the database query result. If no limit is specified,
Returns

A pandas DataFrame is being returned by the get_query_to_df function.

def get_stats( self, table: str = None, table_view: str = None, annotations_stats: bool = False, queries: dict = None, queries_view: str = None) -> dict: 
 812    def get_stats(
 813        self,
 814        table: str = None,
 815        table_view: str = None,
 816        annotations_stats: bool = False,
 817        queries: dict = None,
 818        queries_view: str = None,
 819    ) -> dict:
 820        """
 821        Calculate and return various statistics of the current object, including information about the input file,
 822        variants, samples, header fields, quality, and SNVs/InDels.
 823
 824        :param table: The name of the table containing variant data. If not provided, the default table is used.
 825        :type table: str, optional
 826        :param table_view: The name of the table view to be used for statistics calculation. If not provided, a new view is created.
 827        :type table_view: str, optional
 828        :param annotations_stats: Whether to calculate annotation statistics. Defaults to False.
 829        :type annotations_stats: bool, optional
 830        :param queries: The `queries` parameter is a dictionary that contains queries to be executed
 831        and added to the statistics. The keys of the dictionary are the names of the queries, and the
 832        values are the SQL queries to be executed.
 833        :type queries: dict
 834        :param queries_view: The `queries_view` parameter is a string that represents the name of the
 835        view to be used for the queries. If no value is provided, a new view will be created.
 836        :type queries_view: str
 837
 838        :return: A dictionary containing various statistics of the current object. The dictionary has the following structure:
 839
 840            - **Infos** (*dict*): General information about the input file and header fields.
 841                - **Input file** (*str*): The path to the input file.
 842                - **Header Infos** (*list*): List of INFO fields in the header.
 843                - **Header Formats** (*list*): List of FORMAT fields in the header.
 844                - **Number of INFO fields** (*int*): Number of INFO fields in the header.
 845                - **Number of FORMAT fields** (*int*): Number of FORMAT fields in the header.
 846                - **Number of samples** (*int*): Number of samples in the dataset.
 847                - **Number of variants** (*int*): Total number of variants in the dataset.
 848
 849            - **Variants** (*dict*): Statistics about the variants.
 850                - **By Chromosome** (*list*): List of dictionaries with chromosome names and variant counts.
 851                - **By Type** (*list*): List of dictionaries with variant types and counts.
 852                - **By Quality** (*list*): List of dictionaries with quality scores and counts.
 853                - **By Filter** (*list*): List of dictionaries with filter values and counts.
 854
 855            - **Samples** (*dict*): Statistics about the samples.
 856                - **Variants in samples** (*list*): List of dictionaries with sample names, variant counts, and percentages.
 857
 858            - **Header** (*dict*): Detailed information about the header fields.
 859                - **List of INFO fields** (*dict*): Dictionary with detailed information about INFO fields.
 860                - **List of FORMAT fields** (*dict*): Dictionary with detailed information about FORMAT fields.
 861                - **List of FILTER fields** (*dict*): Dictionary with detailed information about FILTER fields.
 862
 863            - **Annotations** (*dict*, optional): Annotation statistics, if `annotations_stats` is True.
 864                - **Stats** (*dict*): Dictionary with annotation statistics.
 865
 866            - **Quality** (*dict*): Quality statistics.
 867                - **QUAL** (*dict*): Dictionary with quality statistics (average, minimum, maximum, standard deviation, median, variance).
 868
 869        :rtype: dict
 870
 871        :example:
 872
 873        .. code-block:: python
 874
 875            stats = get_stats(table="variants_table", table_view="variants_view", annotations_stats=True)
 876            print(stats)
 877        """
 878
 879        # Log
 880        log.info(f"Stats Calculation...")
 881
 882        # table variants
 883        if table is None:
 884            table_variants_from = self.get_table_variants()
 885        else:
 886            table_variants_from = table
 887
 888        # table view
 889        if table_view is None:
 890            variants_view_stats_name = "variants_view_stats_" + get_random()
 891        else:
 892            variants_view_stats_name = table_view
 893
 894        # Tables to remove
 895        tables_to_remove = []
 896
 897        # Percent_round
 898        percent_round = 2
 899
 900        # Sample struct column name
 901        sample_struct_column = "SAMPLES"
 902
 903        # Info struct column name
 904        info_struct_column = None
 905
 906        # Sample struct column format needed
 907        if annotations_stats:
 908            info_prefix_column = ""
 909        else:
 910            info_prefix_column = None
 911
 912        # Create view
 913        variants_view_stats_name = self.create_annotations_view(
 914            table=table_variants_from,
 915            view=variants_view_stats_name,
 916            view_type="table",
 917            view_mode="full",
 918            info_prefix_column=info_prefix_column,
 919            info_struct_column=info_struct_column,
 920            sample_struct_column=sample_struct_column,
 921            formats=["GT"],
 922            fields_needed=[
 923                "#CHROM",
 924                "POS",
 925                "REF",
 926                "ALT",
 927                "QUAL",
 928                "FILTER",
 929            ]
 930            + self.get_header_sample_list(),
 931        )
 932        tables_to_remove.append(variants_view_stats_name)
 933
 934        # stats dict
 935        stats = {"Infos": {}}
 936
 937        ### File
 938        input_file = self.get_input()
 939        stats["Infos"]["Input file"] = input_file
 940
 941        # Header
 942        header_infos = self.get_header().infos
 943        header_formats = self.get_header().formats
 944        header_infos_list = list(header_infos)
 945        header_formats_list = list(header_formats)
 946        header_table = self.load_header()
 947
 948        # Stat section
 949        stats["Stats"] = {}
 950
 951        ### Variants
 952
 953        # Variants by chr
 954        sql_query_nb_variant_by_chrom = f'SELECT "#CHROM" as CHROM, count(*) as count FROM {variants_view_stats_name} GROUP BY "#CHROM"'
 955        df_nb_of_variants_by_chrom = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_nb_variant_by_chrom)
 956        nb_of_variants_by_chrom = df_nb_of_variants_by_chrom.sort_values(
 957            by=["CHROM"], kind="quicksort"
 958        )
 959
 960        # Total number of variants
 961        nb_of_variants = nb_of_variants_by_chrom["count"].sum()
 962
 963        # Calculate percentage
 964        nb_of_variants_by_chrom["percent"] = nb_of_variants_by_chrom["count"].apply(
 965            lambda x: round((x * 100 / nb_of_variants), percent_round)
 966        )
 967
 968        # Add to stats dict the number of variants by chromosome and the total number of variants
 969        stats["Stats"]["Variants by chromosome"] = nb_of_variants_by_chrom.to_dict(
 970            orient="index"
 971        )
 972
 973        # Add to stats dict the total number of variants
 974        stats["Infos"]["Number of variants"] = int(nb_of_variants)
 975
 976        ### Samples
 977
 978        # Init
 979        samples = {}
 980        nb_of_samples = 0
 981
 982        # Check Samples
 983        if "GT" in header_formats_list and "FORMAT" in self.get_header_columns():
 984            log.debug(f"Check samples...")
 985
 986            # Samples stats
 987            samples_stats = {}
 988
 989            # Get samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
 990            for sample in self.get_header_sample_list():
 991                sql_query_samples = f"""
 992                    SELECT 
 993                        '{sample}' as 'sample',
 994                        SAMPLES."{sample}".GT as 'genotype',
 995                        count(SAMPLES."{sample}".GT) as 'count',
 996                        ROUND((count(SAMPLES."{sample}".GT)*100/{nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) as 'percent'
 997                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
 998                    WHERE  SAMPLES."{sample}".GT IS NOT NULL
 999                    GROUP BY genotype
1000                    ORDER BY genotype
1001                """
1002
1003                # Get samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1004                sql_query_genotype_df = self.get_connexion().execute(sql_query_samples).df()
1005                non_null_genotypes = sql_query_genotype_df[
1006                    sql_query_genotype_df["genotype"].str.contains(r"\d")
1007                ]
1008                sample_genotype_count = non_null_genotypes["count"].sum()
1009
1010                # Add to samples dict the samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1011                if len(sql_query_genotype_df):
1012
1013                    # Number of samples
1014                    nb_of_samples += 1
1015
1016                    # Add to samples dict the samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1017                    samples[sample] = sql_query_genotype_df.to_dict(orient="index")
1018
1019                    # Add to samples stats dict the samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1020                    samples_stats[sample] = {
1021                        "Sample": f"{sample}",
1022                        "count": int(sample_genotype_count),
1023                        "percent": round(
1024                            (sample_genotype_count * 100 / nb_of_variants),
1025                            percent_round,
1026                        ),
1027                    }
1028
1029            # Add to stats dict the samples stats by genotype for each sample in the header
1030            stats["Samples"] = samples
1031            stats["Infos"]["Number of samples"] = nb_of_samples
1032            stats["Stats"]["Variants by sample"] = samples_stats
1033
1034        else:
1035
1036            samples_stats = {}
1037
1038        ### INFO and FORMAT fields
1039        header_types_df = {}
1040        header_types_list = {
1041            "INFO": {
1042                "label": "List of INFO fields",
1043                "fields": {
1044                    "id": "INFO",
1045                    "number": "Number",
1046                    "type": "Type",
1047                    "description": "Description",
1048                },
1049            },
1050            "FORMAT": {
1051                "label": "List of FORMAT fields",
1052                "fields": {
1053                    "id": "FORMAT",
1054                    "number": "Number",
1055                    "type": "Type",
1056                    "description": "Description",
1057                },
1058            },
1059            "FILTER": {
1060                "label": "List of FILTER fields",
1061                "fields": {
1062                    "id": "FILTER",
1063                    "description": "Description",
1064                },
1065            },
1066        }
1067
1068        # Init
1069        header_types_df = {}
1070
1071        # Get header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1072        for header_section, header_info in header_types_list.items():
1073            label = header_info["label"]
1074            fields = header_info["fields"]
1075
1076            # Construire la liste des champs à sélectionner
1077            select_fields = ", ".join(fields.keys())
1078
1079            # SQL query
1080            sql_query_header = f"""
1081                SELECT {select_fields}
1082                FROM {header_table}
1083                WHERE section = '{header_section}'
1084            """
1085            header_infos_df = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_header)
1086            header_infos_dict = {}
1087
1088            # Add to header_types_df the header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1089            for i, row in header_infos_df.iterrows():
1090                header_infos_dict[i] = {
1091                    new if new else original: row[original]
1092                    for original, new in fields.items()
1093                }
1094
1095            # Add to header_types_df the header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1096            if len(header_infos_dict):
1097
1098                # Add to header_types_df the header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1099                header_types_df[label] = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(
1100                    header_infos_dict, orient="index"
1101                ).to_dict(orient="index")
1102
1103                # Add to stats dict the number of INFO and FORMAT fields
1104                stats["Infos"][f"Number of {header_section} fields"] = len(
1105                    header_types_df[label]
1106                )
1107
1108        # Add to stats dict the header types for INFO and FORMAT fields
1109        stats["Header"] = header_types_df
1110
1111        # Annotations stats
1112        if annotations_stats:
1113
1114            # Init
1115            sql_queries_info = []
1116
1117            # Get header infos list
1118            for field in header_infos_list:
1119
1120                # Create a table with a field by line (only for INFO section), and le number of distinct value on variants table, and the number of variants with a value
1121                sql_queries_info.append(f"""
1122                        SELECT
1123                            '{field}' AS 'Annotation',
1124                            count(distinct "{field}") as 'Distinct values',
1125                            count("{field}") as 'Annotated Variants',
1126                            ROUND((count("{field}") * 100 / {nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) as 'Percent',
1127                        FROM
1128                            {variants_view_stats_name}
1129                        WHERE
1130                            "{field}" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(CAST("{field}" AS VARCHAR)) NOT IN ('','.')
1131                    """)
1132
1133            # Join all queries
1134            sql_query_info = f""" UNION ALL """.join(sql_queries_info)
1135
1136            # Get info stats
1137            info_stats = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_info)
1138
1139            # Add to stats dict the annotations stats
1140            stats["Annotations"] = {"Distribution": info_stats.to_dict(orient="index")}
1141
1142        ### Quality stats
1143        log.debug(f"Quality stats...")
1144
1145        ### QUAL
1146        log.debug(f"Quality stats: QUAL...")
1147
1148        if "QUAL" in self.get_header_columns():
1149
1150            # SQL query
1151            sql_query_qual = f"""
1152                    SELECT
1153                        avg(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Average,
1154                        min(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Minimum,
1155                        max(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Maximum,
1156                        stddev(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS StandardDeviation,
1157                        median(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Median,
1158                        variance(CAST(QUAL AS INTEGER)) AS Variance
1159                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1160                    WHERE CAST(QUAL AS VARCHAR) NOT IN ('.')
1161                    """
1162
1163            # Get quality stats
1164            qual_stats = self.get_connexion().execute(sql_query_qual).df().to_dict(orient="index")
1165
1166        else:
1167
1168            # Empty quality stats
1169            qual_stats = {}
1170
1171        ### FILTER
1172        log.debug(f"Quality stats: FILTER...")
1173
1174        if "FILTER" in self.get_header_columns():
1175
1176            # SQL query
1177            sql_query_filter = f"""
1178                WITH split_filter AS (
1179                    SELECT
1180                        TRIM(UNNEST(STRING_SPLIT(CASE WHEN TRIM(FILTER) = '' OR FILTER IS NULL THEN '.' ELSE FILTER END, ';'))) AS filter_value
1181                    FROM
1182                        {variants_view_stats_name}
1183                )
1184                SELECT
1185                    filter_value,
1186                    COUNT(*) AS 'count',
1187                    ROUND((count * 100 / {nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) AS 'percent'
1188                FROM
1189                    split_filter
1190                GROUP BY
1191                    filter_value
1192                ORDER BY
1193                    count DESC
1194            """
1195
1196            # Get filter stats
1197            filter_stats = (
1198                self.get_connexion().execute(sql_query_filter).df().to_dict(orient="index")
1199            )
1200
1201        else:
1202
1203            # Empty filter stats
1204            filter_stats = {}
1205
1206        ### SNV and InDel
1207
1208        # SQL query
1209        sql_query_snv = f"""
1210            
1211            SELECT Type, count, ROUND((count * 100 / {nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) AS 'percent' FROM (
1212
1213                    SELECT
1214                        'Total' AS Type,
1215                        count(*) AS count
1216                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1217                    
1218                    UNION
1219
1220                    SELECT
1221                        'SNV' AS Type,
1222                        count(*) AS count
1223                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1224                    WHERE len(REF) = 1 AND len(ALT) = 1
1225
1226                    UNION
1227
1228                    SELECT
1229                        'MNV' AS Type,
1230                        count(*) AS count
1231                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1232                    WHERE len(REF) > 1 AND len(ALT) > 1
1233                    AND len(REF) = len(ALT)
1234
1235                    UNION
1236
1237                    SELECT
1238                        'InDel' AS Type,
1239                        count(*) AS count
1240                    FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1241                    WHERE len(REF) > 1 OR len(ALT) > 1
1242                    AND len(REF) != len(ALT)
1243
1244                )
1245
1246            ORDER BY 
1247            CASE
1248                WHEN Type = 'Total' THEN 1
1249                WHEN Type = 'SNV' THEN 2
1250                WHEN Type = 'MNV' THEN 3
1251                WHEN Type = 'InDel' THEN 4
1252            END
1253
1254                """
1255
1256        # Get SNV and InDel stats
1257        snv_indel = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_snv).to_dict(orient="index")
1258
1259        # Substitutions
1260        sql_query_snv_substitution = f"""
1261                SELECT
1262                    concat(REF, '>', ALT) AS 'Substitution',
1263                    count(*) AS count,
1264                    ROUND((count * 100 / {nb_of_variants}), {percent_round}) AS 'percent'
1265                FROM {variants_view_stats_name}
1266                WHERE len(REF) = 1 AND len(ALT) = 1
1267                GROUP BY REF, ALT
1268                ORDER BY count(*) DESC
1269                """
1270        snv_substitution = self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_snv_substitution).to_dict(
1271            orient="index"
1272        )
1273
1274        # Add to stats dict the SNV and InDel stats
1275        stats["Stats"]["Variant types"] = snv_indel
1276        stats["Stats"]["Substitutions"] = snv_substitution
1277        stats["Stats"]["Quality"] = qual_stats
1278        stats["Stats"]["Filters"] = filter_stats
1279
1280        # Queries
1281        if queries is not None:
1282
1283            # Create full annotations view
1284            variants_view_query_name = queries_view
1285            variants_view_query_name = self.create_annotations_view(
1286                table=table_variants_from,
1287                view=variants_view_query_name,
1288                view_type="view",
1289                view_mode="explore",
1290                info_prefix_column="",
1291                info_struct_column="INFOS",
1292                sample_struct_column="SAMPLES",
1293                formats=None,
1294                fields_needed_all=True,
1295                drop_view=True,
1296            )
1297            if queries_view is not None:
1298                tables_to_remove.append(variants_view_query_name)
1299
1300            # Stats queries section
1301            stats["Queries"] = {}
1302
1303            # For each query
1304            for query_infos in queries.items():
1305
1306                # Query name and query
1307                query_name = query_infos[0]
1308                query = query_infos[1]
1309
1310                # Query cast
1311                query_cast = cast_columns_query(query=query, conn=self.get_connexion())
1312
1313                # Query execute
1314                query_res = self.get_query_to_df(query_cast).to_dict(orient="index")
1315                stats["Queries"][query_name] = query_res
1316
1317        # Remove table or view
1318        self.remove_tables_or_views(tables=tables_to_remove)
1319
1320        return stats

Calculate and return various statistics of the current object, including information about the input file, variants, samples, header fields, quality, and SNVs/InDels.

Parameters
  • table: The name of the table containing variant data. If not provided, the default table is used.
  • table_view: The name of the table view to be used for statistics calculation. If not provided, a new view is created.
  • annotations_stats: Whether to calculate annotation statistics. Defaults to False.
  • queries: The queries parameter is a dictionary that contains queries to be executed and added to the statistics. The keys of the dictionary are the names of the queries, and the values are the SQL queries to be executed.
  • queries_view: The queries_view parameter is a string that represents the name of the view to be used for the queries. If no value is provided, a new view will be created.
Returns

A dictionary containing various statistics of the current object. The dictionary has the following structure:

- **Infos** (*dict*): General information about the input file and header fields.
    - **Input file** (*str*): The path to the input file.
    - **Header Infos** (*list*): List of INFO fields in the header.
    - **Header Formats** (*list*): List of FORMAT fields in the header.
    - **Number of INFO fields** (*int*): Number of INFO fields in the header.
    - **Number of FORMAT fields** (*int*): Number of FORMAT fields in the header.
    - **Number of samples** (*int*): Number of samples in the dataset.
    - **Number of variants** (*int*): Total number of variants in the dataset.

- **Variants** (*dict*): Statistics about the variants.
    - **By Chromosome** (*list*): List of dictionaries with chromosome names and variant counts.
    - **By Type** (*list*): List of dictionaries with variant types and counts.
    - **By Quality** (*list*): List of dictionaries with quality scores and counts.
    - **By Filter** (*list*): List of dictionaries with filter values and counts.

- **Samples** (*dict*): Statistics about the samples.
    - **Variants in samples** (*list*): List of dictionaries with sample names, variant counts, and percentages.

- **Header** (*dict*): Detailed information about the header fields.
    - **List of INFO fields** (*dict*): Dictionary with detailed information about INFO fields.
    - **List of FORMAT fields** (*dict*): Dictionary with detailed information about FORMAT fields.
    - **List of FILTER fields** (*dict*): Dictionary with detailed information about FILTER fields.

- **Annotations** (*dict*, optional): Annotation statistics, if `annotations_stats` is True.
    - **Stats** (*dict*): Dictionary with annotation statistics.

- **Quality** (*dict*): Quality statistics.
    - **QUAL** (*dict*): Dictionary with quality statistics (average, minimum, maximum, standard deviation, median, variance).

:example:

stats = get_stats(table="variants_table", table_view="variants_view", annotations_stats=True)
print(stats)

1959        """
1960        The `load_data` function reads a VCF file and inserts it into a table, with options to drop the

1962
1963        :param input_file: The path to the input file. This is the VCF file that will be loaded into the
1964        table
1965        :type input_file: str

1968        `True`, the variants table will be dropped. If set to `False` (default), the variants table will
1969        not be dropped, defaults to False
1970        :type drop_variants_table: bool (optional)
1971        :param sample_size: The `sample_size` parameter determines the number of rows to be sampled from
1972        the input file. If it is set to `None`, the default value of 20480 will be used, defaults to
1973        20480

1975        """
1976
1977        log.info("Loading...")
1978
1979        # change input file
1980        if input_file:
1981            self.set_input(input_file)
1982            self.set_header()
1983
1984        # drop variants table
1985        if drop_variants_table:
1986            self.drop_variants_table()
1987
1988        # get table variants
1989        table_variants = self.get_table_variants()

1993        access = self.get_access(default=None)

1996        # Input format and compress

2001

2010        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
2011
2012        # Sample size
2013        if not sample_size:
2014            sample_size = -1
2015        log.debug(f"sample_size: {sample_size}")
2016
2017        # Load data
2018        log.debug(f"Load Data from {input_format}")
2019
2020        # DuckDB connexion
2021        if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
2022
2023            # Database already exists
2024            if input_format in ["db", "duckdb"]:
2025
2026                if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
2027                    log.debug(f"Input file format '{input_format}' duckDB")
2028                else:
2029                    log.error(
2030                        f"Input file format '{input_format}' not compatilbe with database format '{connexion_format}'"
2031                    )
2032                    raise ValueError(
2033                        f"Input file format '{input_format}' not compatilbe with database format '{connexion_format}'"
2034                    )
2035
2036            # Load from existing database format
2037            else:
2038
2039                try:
2040                    # Create Table or View
2041                    database = Database(database=self.input)
2042                    sql_from = database.get_sql_from(sample_size=sample_size)
2043
2044                    log.debug(f"Load Data into {table_variants}...")
2045                    if access in ["RO"]:
2046                        sql_load = (

2048                        )
2049                    else:
2050                        sql_load = (

2052                        )
2053                    self.get_connexion().execute(sql_load)
2054                    log.debug(f"Load Data into {table_variants} - done.")
2055
2056                except Exception as e:

2059                    log.error(msg_err)
2060                    raise ValueError(msg_err)
2061
2062        # SQLite connexion

2064            "vcf",
2065            "tsv",
2066            "csv",
2067            "psv",
2068        ]:
2069
2070            # Main structure

2136            raise ValueError(
