Update dest_table using multiple sources via CTAS.

Parameters
  • dest_table: The dest_table parameter is a string that represents the name of the destination table that you want to update.
  • sources: The sources parameter is a list of dictionaries, where each dictionary represents a source table and the columns to be updated in the destination table. Each dictionary should have the following keys:
    • "table": The name of the source table.
    • "join_keys": A list of column names that will be used to join the source table with the destination table.
    • "columns": A dictionary where the keys are the destination column names and the values are dictionaries with the following keys:
      • "columns": A list of column names from the source table that will be used to update the destination column.
      • "mode": The mode of updating the column, either "append" or "replace".
      • "separator": The separator to use when appending values (only applicable for "append" mode). sources example: sources = [ { # Default source to append INFO column with a table source as a view "table": "calculation_view_name", "join_keys": ["#CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT"], "columns": { "INFO": {"columns": ["INFO"], "mode": "append", "separator": ";"} }, }, { # Calculation view source to update INFO, and create AF and ALT columns "table": "calculation_view_name", "join_keys": ["#CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT"], "columns": { "INFO": {"columns": ["INFO"], "mode": "append", "separator": ";"}, "AF": {"columns": ["REF"], "mode": "replace"}, "ALT": {"columns": ["REF"], "mode": "replace"}, }, }, { # Clinvar source to add in a new column CLINVAR with concatenation of 2 columns CLNSIG and CLNID "table": "clinvar_table", "join_keys": ["#CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT"], "columns": { "CLINVAR": {"columns": ["CLNSIG", "CLNID"], "mode": "append", "separator": "|"}, }, }, ]
  • mode: The mode parameter determines how the columns in the destination table will be updated. It can take two values: "append" or "replace". The default value is "append".
    • If mode is set to "append", the values from the source tables will be concatenated to the existing values in the destination table, separated by the specified separator.
    • If mode is set to "replace", the values from the source tables will replace the existing values in the destination table.
  • separator: The separator parameter is a string that specifies the character or sequence of characters used to separate values when appending them together. The default value is a semicolon (";"). This parameter is only applicable when the mode parameter is set to "append".
  • physical_order: The physical_order parameter is a boolean value that determines whether the resulting table should have a physical order based on the row number. If set to True, a _rowid column will be added to the resulting table, which will contain the row number for each row. If set to False, the _rowid column will not be included. The default value is True.
  • cleanup: The cleanup parameter is a boolean value that determines whether to drop the temporary table created during the update process. If set to True, the temporary table will be dropped after the update is complete. If set to False, the temporary table will be retained. The default value is False.
  • strategy: The strategy parameter determines the method used to update the destination table. It can take two values: "ctas" or "merge". The default value is "ctas".
    • If strategy is set to "ctas", the update will be performed using a "Create Table As Select" (CTAS) approach. This involves creating a new temporary table with the updated data and then replacing the original table with the temporary table.
    • If strategy is set to "update", the update will be performed using an "UPDATE" statement. This involves directly modifying the existing rows in the destination table based on the data from the source tables.
  • chunking: The chunking parameter is a boolean value that determines whether to process the update operation in chunks or not. If set to True, the update will be performed in smaller chunks of data, which can help improve performance and reduce memory usage. If set to False, the update will be performed on the entire dataset at once. The default value is True.
  • chunk_size: The chunk_size parameter is an optional integer that specifies the size of the chunks to be processed during the update operation. If not provided, it will default to a value from the configuration file or a predefined constant DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE.
  • upper_case: The upper_case parameter is a boolean value that determines whether to convert the values of the join keys to uppercase before performing the join operation. If set to True, the join keys will be converted to uppercase using the upper function. If set to False, the join keys will be used as they are. The default value is False.
  • chromosomes: The chromosomes parameter is a list of chromosome names (strings) that can be used to filter the data during the update process. If provided, only the rows corresponding to the specified chromosomes will be considered for the update. If not provided, all chromosomes will be included in the update process.
Returns

The function update_table does not return anything. It performs an update operation on a destination table using multiple source tables and their specified columns.

def annotation_format_to_table( self, annotation_field: str = 'ANN', annotation_id: str = 'Feature_ID', view_name: str = 'transcripts', view_type: str = 'view', column_rename: dict = {}, column_clean: bool = False, column_case: str = None, column_split: str = '&') -> str: 
4993    def annotation_format_to_table(
4994        self,
4995        annotation_field: str = "ANN",
4996        annotation_id: str = "Feature_ID",

5004        """
5005        Converts annotation data from a VCF file into a structured table format, ensuring unique values
5006        and creating a temporary table for further processing or analysis.
5007
5008        Args:
5009            annotation_field (str, optional): The field in the VCF file that contains the annotation information
5010                for each variant. Defaults to "ANN".
5011            annotation_id (str, optional): The identifier for the annotation feature, used as a column name
5012                in the resulting table or view. Defaults to "Feature_ID".
5013            view_name (str, optional): The name of the temporary table that will be created to store the transformed
5014                annotation data. Defaults to "transcripts".
5015            view_type (str, optional): The type of the view to be created. Defaults to "view".
5016            column_rename (dict, optional): A dictionary to specify custom renaming for columns. By providing key-value
5017                pairs in this dictionary, you can rename specific columns in the resulting table or view.
5018            column_clean (bool, optional): A flag to determine whether the annotation field should undergo a cleaning process.
5019                If set to True, the function will clean the annotation field before further processing. Defaults to False.
5020            column_case (str, optional): Specifies the case transformation to be applied to the column names extracted from
5021                the annotation data. It allows you to set the case of the column names to either lowercase or uppercase.
5022            column_split (str, optional): The separator to split field values. Defaults to "&". Set to None to disable splitting.
5023
5024        Returns:
5025            str: The name of the view created, which is stored in the variable `view_name`.
5026        """
5027
5028        # annotation_id original name
5029        annotation_id_original = annotation_id
5030
5031        # Transcript annotation
5032        if column_rename:
5033            annotation_id = column_rename.get(annotation_id, annotation_id)
5034
5035        if column_clean:
5036            annotation_id = clean_annotation_field(annotation_id)
5037
5038        # Prefix
5039        prefix = self.get_explode_infos_prefix()
5040        if prefix:
5041            prefix = "INFO/"
5042
5043        # Variants table
5044        table_variants = self.get_table_variants()
5045
5046        # Header
5047        vcf_reader = self.get_header()
5048
5049        # Add columns
5050        added_columns = []
5051        added_columns_type = {}
5052
5053        # If annotation_field exists
5054        if annotation_field in vcf_reader.infos:
5055
5056            # Extract ANN header
5057            ann_description = vcf_reader.infos[annotation_field].desc
5058            pattern = r"'(.+?)'"
5059            match = re.search(pattern, ann_description)
5060            if match:
5061                ann_header_match = match.group(1).split(" | ")
5062                ann_header = []
5063                ann_header_desc = {}
5064                for i in range(len(ann_header_match)):
5065                    ann_header_info = "".join(
5066                        char for char in ann_header_match[i] if char.isalnum()
5067                    )
5068                    ann_header.append(ann_header_info)
5069                    ann_header_desc[ann_header_info] = ann_header_match[i]
5070                if not ann_header_desc:
5071                    raise ValueError("Invalid header description format")
5072            else:
5073                raise ValueError("Invalid header description format")
5074
5075            # annotation field pattern
5076            annotation_field_pattern = rf"(^|;)({annotation_field})=([^;]*)?"
5077
5078            annotation_fields_for_format = []
5079            for i, header in enumerate(ann_header_desc.values()):
5080                if header in [annotation_id_original]:
5081                    annotation_fields_for_format.append(
5082                        f"SPLIT_PART(annotation, '|', {i+1}) AS '{header}'"
5083                    )
5084                else:
5085                    annotation_fields_for_format.append(
5086                        f"string_agg(SPLIT_PART(annotation, '|', {i+1}), ',') AS '{header}'"
5087                    )
5088
5089            query = f""" 
5090                WITH exploded_annotations AS (
5091                    SELECT
5092                        "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,
5093                        UNNEST(
5094                            STRING_SPLIT(
5095                                regexp_extract("INFO", '{annotation_field_pattern}', 3),
5096                                ','
5097                            )
5098                        ) AS annotation
5099                    FROM {table_variants}
5100                ),
5101                split_annotations AS (
5102                    SELECT
5103                        "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,
5104                        {", ".join(annotation_fields_for_format)}
5105                    FROM exploded_annotations
5106                    GROUP BY "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT, "{annotation_id_original}"
5107                )
5108                SELECT * FROM split_annotations
5109                LIMIT 10000
5110                """
5111            dataframe_annotation_format = self.get_query_to_df(query=query)
5112
5113            # Init
5114            query_list_keys = []
5115            key_i = 0
5116
5117            for key in dataframe_annotation_format.keys():
5118
5119                if key in ann_header_desc.values():
5120
5121                    # Key
5122                    key_i += 1
5123                    key_clean = key
5124
5125                    # key rename
5126                    if column_rename:
5127                        key_clean = column_rename.get(key_clean, key_clean)
5128
5129                    # key clean
5130                    if column_clean:
5131                        key_clean = clean_annotation_field(key_clean)
5132
5133                    # Key case
5134                    if column_case:

5137                        elif column_case.lower() in ["upper"]:
5138                            key_clean = key_clean.upper()
5139

5141                    column_type = detect_column_type(dataframe_annotation_format[key])
5142                    added_columns_type[key] = column_type
5143                    log.debug(f"Field '{key}' type detected: {column_type}")
5144
5145                    # Append key to list
5146                    if column_split is not None:
5147                        query_list_keys.append(
5148                            f""" TRY_CAST(replace(NULLIF(SPLIT_PART(annotation, '|', {key_i}), ''), '{column_split}', ',') AS {column_type}) AS '{prefix}{key_clean}' """
5149                        )
5150                    else:
5151                        query_list_keys.append(
5152                            f""" TRY_CAST(NULLIF(SPLIT_PART(annotation, '|', {key_i}), '') AS {column_type}) AS '{prefix}{key_clean}' """
5153                        )
5154
5155            # Create temporary table
5156            query_create_view = f"""
5157                CREATE {view_type} {view_name} AS (
5158                    WITH exploded_annotations AS (
5159                        SELECT
5160                            "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,
5161                            UNNEST(
5162                                STRING_SPLIT(
5163                                    regexp_extract("INFO", '{annotation_field_pattern}', 3),
5164                                    ','
5165                                )
5166                            ) AS annotation
5167                        FROM {table_variants}
5168                    ),
5169                    split_annotations AS (
5170                        SELECT
5171                            "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,
5172                            {", ".join(query_list_keys)},
5173                        FROM exploded_annotations
5174                    )
5175                    SELECT *, {annotation_id} AS 'transcript' FROM split_annotations
5176                )
5177            """
5178            # log.debug(f"Create view FORMAT:{query_create_view}")
5179            self.execute_query(query=query_create_view)
5180
5181        else:
5182
5183            # Return None
5184            view_name = None
5185
5186        return view_name, added_columns, added_columns_type

Converts annotation data from a VCF file into a structured table format, ensuring unique values and creating a temporary table for further processing or analysis.

Args: annotation_field (str, optional): The field in the VCF file that contains the annotation information for each variant. Defaults to "ANN". annotation_id (str, optional): The identifier for the annotation feature, used as a column name in the resulting table or view. Defaults to "Feature_ID". view_name (str, optional): The name of the temporary table that will be created to store the transformed annotation data. Defaults to "transcripts". view_type (str, optional): The type of the view to be created. Defaults to "view". column_rename (dict, optional): A dictionary to specify custom renaming for columns. By providing key-value pairs in this dictionary, you can rename specific columns in the resulting table or view. column_clean (bool, optional): A flag to determine whether the annotation field should undergo a cleaning process. If set to True, the function will clean the annotation field before further processing. Defaults to False. column_case (str, optional): Specifies the case transformation to be applied to the column names extracted from the annotation data. It allows you to set the case of the column names to either lowercase or uppercase. column_split (str, optional): The separator to split field values. Defaults to "&". Set to None to disable splitting.

Returns: str: The name of the view created, which is stored in the variable view_name.

5195        """

5207        specified fields in the VCF file header

5210        the original field names as keys and their corresponding new names (or None if the field was
5211        removed) as values after renaming or removing specified fields in a VCF file header and updating
5212        corresponding INFO fields in the variants table.
5213        """
5214
5215        # Config
5216        config = self.get_config()
5217
5218        # Access
5219        # access = config.get("access")
5220        access = self.get_access(default=None)
5221
5222        # Init
5223        fields_processed = {
5224            "renamed": {},
5225            "removed": {},
5226            "not_processed": {},
5227            "not_found": {},
5228        }
5229
5230        if table is None:
5231            table = self.get_table_variants()
5232
5233        # Clasue case

5235

5238
5239        # For each field to rename or remove, one by one
5240        if fields_to_rename is not None:
5241            for field_to_rename, field_renamed in fields_to_rename.items():
5242
5243                # If no field to process
5244                if field_to_rename != "":
5245
5246                    # rename empty is remove
5247                    if field_renamed == "":
5248                        field_renamed = None
5249
5250                    # Check if already to process
5251                    check_field_to_rename_found = False
5252                    for (
5253                        field_to_process_to_rename,
5254                        field_to_process_renamed,
5255                    ) in fields_to_process.items():
5256                        if field_to_rename == field_to_process_renamed:
5257                            # Replace filed to process
5258                            fields_to_process[field_to_process_to_rename] = (
5259                                field_renamed
5260                            )
5261                            check_field_to_rename_found = True
5262                    if not check_field_to_rename_found:
5263                        # Add field to process
5264                        fields_to_process[field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5265
5266        if len(fields_to_process) and access not in ["RO"]:
5267
5268            # Log
5269            log.info("Rename or remove fields...")
5270
5271            # Header
5272            header = self.get_header()
5273
5274            # For each field
5275            for field_to_rename, field_renamed in fields_to_process.items():
5276
5277                # If to rename or remove
5278                if (
5279                    field_to_rename != field_renamed
5280                    and field_to_rename not in ["", None]
5281                    and field_renamed not in [""]
5282                ):
5283
5284                    # Rename
5285                    if field_renamed is not None:
5286
5287                        # Case clause
5288                        clause_case.append(
5289                            f""" WHEN k = '{field_to_rename}' THEN '{field_renamed}'  """
5290                        )
5291
5292                        # Fields processed
5293                        fields_processed["renamed"][field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5294
5295                        # Log

5298                        )
5299
5300                    # Remove
5301                    else:
5302
5303                        # Case clause
5304                        clause_case.append(
5305                            f""" WHEN k = '{field_to_rename}' THEN NULL  """
5306                        )
5307
5308                        # Fields processed
5309                        fields_processed["removed"][field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5310
5311                        # Log
5312                        log.debug(
5313                            f"Rename or remove fields - field '{field_to_rename}' removed"
5314                        )
5315
5316                    # Header
5317                    if field_to_rename in header.infos:
5318
5319                        # Rename header if to rename
5320                        if field_renamed is not None:
5321                            header.infos[field_renamed] = vcf.parser._Info(
5322                                field_renamed,
5323                                header.infos[field_to_rename].num,
5324                                header.infos[field_to_rename].type,
5325                                header.infos[field_to_rename].desc,
5326                                header.infos[field_to_rename].source,
5327                                header.infos[field_to_rename].version,
5328                                header.infos[field_to_rename].type_code,
5329                            )
5330
5331                        # Remove header, if rename or remove
5332                        del header.infos[field_to_rename]
5333
5334                    else:
5335
5336                        # Log
5337                        log.warning(
5338                            f"Rename or remove fields - field '{field_to_rename}' not in header"
5339                        )
5340
5341                        # Fields processed
5342                        fields_processed["not_found"][field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5343
5344                else:
5345
5346                    # Fields processed
5347                    fields_processed["not_pocessed"][field_to_rename] = field_renamed
5348
5349            # Process
5350            if len(clause_case):
5351
5352                # Update query
5353                query_update = f"""
5354                    UPDATE {table}
5355                    SET INFO = renamed_table.INFO                       -- update INFO
5356                    FROM (
5357                        SELECT
5358                            "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,                    -- variant id
5359                            IFNULL(string_agg(kv, ';'), '.') AS INFO    -- INFO
5360                        FROM (
5361                            SELECT
5362                                "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,                -- variant id
5363                                CASE
5364                                    WHEN k IS NOT NULL                  -- key not null
5365                                    THEN
5366                                        CASE 
5367                                            WHEN v IS NOT NULL          -- value not null
5368                                            THEN concat(k, '=', v)      -- key-value: either String, Integer, Float
5369                                            ELSE k                      -- Flag
5370                                        END
5371                                    ELSE NULL                           -- remove
5372                                END AS kv
5373                            FROM (
5374                                SELECT "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,         -- variant id
5375                                    CASE
5376                                        {" ".join(clause_case)}         -- rename or remove
5377                                        ELSE k                          -- no change
5378                                    END AS k,                           -- key
5379                                    v                                   -- value
5380                                FROM (
5381                                    SELECT
5382                                        "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT,        -- variant id
5383                                        string_split(kv, '=')[1] AS k,  -- key
5384                                        string_split(kv, '=')[2] AS v   -- value
5385                                    FROM (
5386                                        SELECT "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT, unnest(string_split(INFO, ';')) AS kv
5387                                        FROM variants
5388                                        )
5389                                    )
5390                                )
5391                            )
5392                        GROUP BY "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT
5393                    ) AS renamed_table
5394                    WHERE {table}."#CHROM" = renamed_table."#CHROM"     -- join
5395                    AND {table}."POS" = renamed_table."POS"
5396                    AND {table}."REF" = renamed_table."REF"
5397                    AND {table}."ALT" = renamed_table."ALT"
5398                """
5399                # log.debug(f"query_update={query_update}")
5400                self.execute_query(query_update)
5401
5402        return fields_processed

The calculation_recreate_info_fields function retrieves parameters from a dictionary, recreate INFO fields with rename and table if provided, and then calls another function to rename the fields.

Parameters
  • fields_to_rename: fields_to_rename is a dictionary that contains the fields to be renamed in a table. Each key-value pair in the dictionary represents the original field name as the key and the new field name as the value
  • table: The table parameter in the calculation_recreate_info_fields method is used to specify the name of the table for which the fields are to be renamed. It is a string type parameter
  • operation_name: The operation_name parameter in the calculation_recreate_info_fields method is a string that specifies the name of the operation being performed. In this context, it is used as a default value for the operation name if not explicitly provided when calling the function, defaults to RENAME_INFO_FIELDS
